# M01 — I01 Establish Authoritative Scientific Configuration Contract

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M01 — Authoritative Scientific Contract and Repository Foundation
- **Primary deliverable:** Immutable typed `configs/fedorbit.yaml` contract with single-source scientific authority.
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure
- **Requirement coverage:** 176 total (176 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- Document authority; §§4–4.1
- Configuration YAML and configuration-adjacent label identity across §§4.2–4.4, 4.8–4.21, 4.23, 4.25, and §6.4

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0001–REQ-0003, REQ-0097–REQ-0126, REQ-0132–REQ-0143, REQ-0174–REQ-0193, REQ-0277, REQ-0318–REQ-0328, REQ-0355–REQ-0357, REQ-0376–REQ-0384, REQ-0405–REQ-0412, REQ-0438–REQ-0442, REQ-0446–REQ-0456, REQ-0485–REQ-0497, REQ-0507–REQ-0511, REQ-0548–REQ-0555, REQ-0608, REQ-0653, REQ-0658–REQ-0660, REQ-0697–REQ-0705, REQ-0728–REQ-0750

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0001** (Document authority; Architecture) — The roadmap is the sole authority for scientific definitions, numerical values, experiment membership, statistical procedures, claim criteria, and implementation semantics.
- **REQ-0002** (Document authority; Architecture) — No implementation mechanism may override a roadmap scientific definition, parameter, metric, test, experiment, baseline budget, claim threshold, or reporting rule.
- **REQ-0003** (Document authority; Reproducibility) — No TEST outcome may alter a scientific definition, parameter, metric, test, experiment, baseline budget, claim threshold, or reporting rule.
- **REQ-0097** (§4; Configuration) — `configs/fedorbit.yaml` must contain configuration data only.
- **REQ-0098** (§4; Configuration) — `configs/fedorbit.yaml` is the sole authority for retained numerical parameters, thresholds, tolerances, counts, fractions, seeds, experiment-grid values, dataset/path identifiers, and other genuine configurable selections.
- **REQ-0099** (§4; Architecture) — Fixed mathematical definitions, algorithm procedures, validation rules, execution semantics, deterministic ordering, architecture definitions, failure behavior, provenance rules, and reporting semantics must remain authoritative in roadmap prose rather than being encoded as YAML prose or pseudo-expressions.
- **REQ-0100** (§4; Configuration) — Observed raw-data facts, derived quantities, and runtime measurements must remain outside production YAML.
- **REQ-0101** (§4.1; Configuration) — Configuration-data values are primitive supplied/selected/varied values; registered principal values, confirmatory thresholds, seeds, and grids may vary only where the roadmap explicitly defines a sensitivity or experiment grid.
- **REQ-0102** (§4.1; Dataset) — Observed raw-data facts must be measured from immutable raw data and recorded in dataset manifests; literature expectations may not replace them.
- **REQ-0103** (§4.1; Configuration) — Derived quantities must be deterministically computed from configuration data, fixed rules, or observed inputs and must not be independently configurable.
- **REQ-0104** (§4.1; Reproducibility) — Runtime measurements must be measured outcomes and must never be predetermined as configuration.

## Objective

Deliver Immutable typed `configs/fedorbit.yaml` contract with single-source scientific authority so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

- **Document authority; §§4–4.1 — Roadmap authority, configuration-data ownership, and typed-contract boundary.**

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M01 — Authoritative Scientific Contract and Repository Foundation

- **Issue type:** Infrastructure

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §§4.22, 4.26–4.28

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0685–REQ-0696, REQ-0785–REQ-0790, REQ-0799–REQ-0821

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0685** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Principal model execution requires CUDA.
- **REQ-0686** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Enable `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` for principal execution.
- **REQ-0687** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Disable cuDNN benchmark mode for principal execution.
- **REQ-0688** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Enable cuDNN deterministic mode for principal execution.
- **REQ-0689** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Disable TF32 for matrix multiplication during principal execution.
- **REQ-0690** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Disable TF32 for cuDNN during principal execution.
- **REQ-0691** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Disable stochastic mixed precision during principal execution.
- **REQ-0692** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Disable automatic mixed precision during principal execution.
- **REQ-0693** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Keep model training float32 during principal execution.
- **REQ-0694** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Synchronize CUDA around timed GPU regions.
- **REQ-0695** (§4.22; Testing) — Smoke and unit tests may use CPU.
- **REQ-0696** (§4.22; Reproducibility) — Any operation unable to satisfy deterministic execution is prohibited from principal execution unless the roadmap explicitly defines a repeatability tolerance.
- **REQ-0785** (§4.26; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `runtime.reference_model_gpu` exactly to `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB`.
- **REQ-0786** (§4.26; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `runtime.solver_cpu_worker_ceiling` exactly to `4`.
- **REQ-0787** (§4.26; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `runtime.host_ram_ceiling_gib_for_registered_efficiency_runs` exactly to `16`.
- **REQ-0788** (§4.26; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `runtime.deterministic_kernel_warmups` exactly to `3`.
- **REQ-0789** (§4.26; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `runtime.deterministic_kernel_timed_repetitions` exactly to `10`.
- **REQ-0790** (§4.26; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `runtime.full_training_timing_repetitions_per_scientific_cell` exactly to `1`.
- **REQ-0799** (§4.27; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `environment.python` exactly to `3.13.15`.
- **REQ-0800** (§4.27; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `environment.pytorch` exactly to `2.13.0`.

- **REQ-0802** (§4.27; Configuration YAML; Reproducibility) — Set `environment.scipy` exactly to `1.18.0`.

# M01 — I05 Enforce Canonical Repository Architecture and Package Boundaries

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M01 — Authoritative Scientific Contract and Repository Foundation
- **Primary deliverable:** Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests.
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure
- **Requirement coverage:** 434 total (434 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §19.1

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-2041–REQ-2474

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-2041** (§19.1; Architecture) — Provide a typed mirror of the scientific contract in implementation.
- **REQ-2042** (§19.1; Architecture) — Separate data, model, response, correspondence, solver, experiment, metric, statistical, reporting, and provenance responsibilities sufficiently to enforce the roadmap.
- **REQ-2043** (§19.1; Architecture) — Treat the typed scientific configuration as an implementation mirror, never as an independent scientific authority.
- **REQ-2044** (§19.1; Testing) — CI must serialize the typed scientific configuration and fail if it diverges from the roadmap-maintained expected scientific-contract snapshot.
- **REQ-2045** (§19.1; Configuration) — Do not permit ad-hoc YAML scientific overrides.
- **REQ-2046** (§19.1; Configuration) — Do not permit TOML scientific overrides.
- **REQ-2047** (§19.1; Configuration) — Do not permit environment-variable scientific overrides.
- **REQ-2048** (§19.1; Configuration) — Do not permit notebook-setting scientific overrides.
- **REQ-2049** (§19.1; Configuration) — Do not permit any other scientific override mechanism outside the authoritative production configuration.
- **REQ-2050** (§19.1; Testing) — Confine `configs/tests.yml` and `configs/smoke.yml` to automated test/smoke execution; they cannot override production scientific configuration.
- **REQ-2051** (§19.1; Reproducibility) — Repository must contain a fully resolved dependency lock with transitive versions and package hashes.
- **REQ-2052** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover scientific primitives.
- **REQ-2053** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover leakage/resource isolation.
- **REQ-2054** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover solver correctness.
- **REQ-2055** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover deterministic execution.
- **REQ-2056** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover schemas.
- **REQ-2057** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover artifact validity.
- **REQ-2058** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover selective invalidation.
- **REQ-2059** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover recovery.
- **REQ-2060** (§19.1; Testing) — Repository tests must cover CLI behavior.
- **REQ-2061** (§19.1; Architecture) — Expose immutable raw data through `data/raw`.
- **REQ-2062** (§19.1; Artifact) — Write generated computational artifacts only under `outputs/` and manuscript evidence under `results/` according to the lineage contracts.
- **REQ-2063** (§19.1; Provenance) — Repository commit identifies implementation revision for provenance but must never be the sole artifact-validity key.
- **REQ-2064** (§19.1; Provenance) — Govern artifact reuse/invalidation by the stage-specific dependency fingerprints in §§20–21.
- **REQ-2065** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Architecture) — Provide required repository file `project/README.md`. Its responsibility is: Documents FedORBIT's scope, setup, public CLI workflows, experiment execution, artifact policy, and reproducibility procedure.
- **REQ-2066** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Architecture) — Provide required repository file `project/pyproject.toml`. Its responsibility is: Defines package metadata, dependencies, the fedorbit CLI entry point, and linting, typing, and test-tool configuration.
- **REQ-2067** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Reproducibility) — Provide required repository file `project/uv.lock`. Its responsibility is: Locks the complete transitive Python dependency environment and package hashes required for reproducible execution.
- **REQ-2068** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Architecture) — Provide required repository file `project/noxfile.py`. Its responsibility is: Defines repeatable lint, type-check, unit, scientific, integration, architecture, and smoke-test sessions.
- **REQ-2069** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Architecture) — Provide required repository file `project/Makefile`. Its responsibility is: Provides concise developer and operator commands that delegate to the public CLI and repository quality tooling.
- **REQ-2070** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Architecture) — Provide required repository file `project/.gitignore`. Its responsibility is: Excludes generated outputs, caches, local environments, temporary files, and other machine-specific state.
- **REQ-2071** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Configuration) — Provide required repository directory `project/configs/`.
- **REQ-2072** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Configuration) — Provide required repository file `project/configs/fedorbit.yaml`. Its responsibility is: Sole production YAML containing the roadmap-defined numerical parameters, thresholds, seeds, experiment grids, paths, and runtime limits.
- **REQ-2073** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Configuration) — Provide required repository file `project/configs/tests.yml`. Its responsibility is: Provides a small deterministic configuration used exclusively by automated tests.
- **REQ-2074** (§19.1 — Required repository layout; Configuration) — Provide required repository file `project/configs/smoke.yml`. Its responsibility is: Provides the minimal scientifically valid configuration used by the smoke workflow.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue must trace to the roadmap authority above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy it.

## Objective

Deliver Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§19.1 — Repository architecture, package boundaries, canonical paths, and structural enforcement.**
  - Required verification: Repository-tree, import-boundary, AST/static, naming, dead-code, primitive-leak, and architecture tests enforce the required layout and responsibility boundaries.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- **M01 — I01 Establish Authoritative Scientific Configuration Contract** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Immutable typed `configs/fedorbit.yaml` contract with single-source scientific authority.

### Blocks

- **M01 — I06 Enforce Nonclaim Test Boundaries and Scientific-Contract Readiness** — provides Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Nonclaim test/smoke boundary and executable M01 scientific-contract readiness gates.
- **M02 — I07 Implement Deterministic RNG and Reproducibility Identity** — provides Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Deterministic seed namespaces, replay behavior, and reproducibility/environment identity.
- **M02 — I08 Implement Canonical Artifact Reuse and Completion Manifests** — provides Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Reusable-artifact and completion manifests with dependency-aware immutable artifact reuse.
- **M02 — I10 Implement Public CLI Idempotency, Status, and Overwrite Semantics** — provides Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Roadmap-defined public CLI execution surface with validated idempotent status/overwrite behavior.
- **M02 — I12 Implement Canonical Workspace, Serialization, and Provenance Lifecycle** — provides Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Canonical computational workspace and validated artifact/provenance lifecycle.
- **M03 — I14 Enforce Strict No-Common-Interface Resource Boundary** — provides Roadmap-mandated repository tree, dependency boundaries, and structural enforcement tests as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Whitelisted strict-resource interface with dynamic access validation and readiness gates.

Dependencies describe the actual contract or evidence exchanged between issues; dependency completion alone is insufficient unless the consumed output is valid, current, provenance-compatible, and scientifically admissible.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Repository architecture, package boundaries, canonical paths, and structural enforcement.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Add or extend only the typed immutable domain/configuration contracts required by the covered requirements.
- Validate cross-field invariants and reject unknown or scientifically invalid values before execution.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Repository-tree, import-boundary, AST/static, naming, dead-code, primitive-leak, and architecture tests enforce the required layout and responsibility boundaries.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

# M01 — I06 Enforce Nonclaim Test Boundaries and Scientific-Contract Readiness

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M01 — Authoritative Scientific Contract and Repository Foundation
- **Primary deliverable:** Nonclaim test/smoke boundary and executable M01 scientific-contract readiness gates.
- **Issue type:** Validation
- **Requirement coverage:** 17 total (17 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.29
- §26

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0827–REQ-0840, REQ-3172–REQ-3173, REQ-3182

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0827** (§4.29; Testing) — `configs/tests.yml` and `configs/smoke.yml` may contain only nonclaim execution-fixture controls.
- **REQ-0828** (§4.29; Testing) — Test/smoke configuration keys must not shadow or override any key under production `scientific`, `solvers`, `generators`, `experiments`, `runtime`, `environment`, or `reporting`.
- **REQ-0829** (§4.29; Testing) — Test/smoke fixture controls may alter only synthetic/tiny fixtures and test-runtime truncation.

## Objective

Deliver Reusable-artifact and completion manifests with dependency-aware immutable artifact reuse so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§15 — Experiment dependency and artifact map — Shared canonical artifact reuse across experiments.**
  - Required verification: Artifact-reference tests prove dependency-fingerprint reuse without duplicate prepared splits, checkpoints, predictions, packets, solver results, confirmations, or other immutable payloads.
- **§22.8–§22.9 — Completion and reusable-artifact manifests.**
  - Required verification: Typed-schema tests validate completion/reusable manifests, payload checksums, dependency references, and stable artifact identity.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.

# M02 — I09 Implement Failure Taxonomy, Retry, and Scientific Failure Semantics

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M02 — Deterministic Execution, Artifact, and Provenance Backbone
- **Primary deliverable:** Typed failure states, retry behavior, and scientific/infrastructure failure handling.
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure
- **Requirement coverage:** 28 total (28 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §18

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-1991–REQ-2018

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-1991** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Treat process crash, filesystem failure, CUDA runtime error, and infrastructure-caused malformed temporary serialization as infrastructure failures.
- **REQ-1992** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Retry an infrastructure failure exactly twice after the initial failed attempt.
- **REQ-1993** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Infrastructure retries must use identical semantic identity and configuration.
- **REQ-1994** (§18; Failure Semantics) — After three total infrastructure failures, terminate as `Failed / Infrastructure Failure`.
- **REQ-1995** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Block dependent cells after terminal infrastructure failure.
- **REQ-1996** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Treat leakage, split overlap, conflicting duplicates, strict-resource violation, configuration mismatch, theorem primitive mismatch, or schema failure as validation failure.
- **REQ-1997** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Use `Invalid` for data/scientific-validity defects and `Failed / Validation Failure` for executable implementation defects.
- **REQ-1998** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A correctly executed unfavorable scientific outcome remains terminal state `Completed`.
- **REQ-1999** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Claim adjudication, not execution status, determines the scientific claim state for a scientific null.
- **REQ-2000** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A correctly executed failure-boundary condition remains `Completed` even when FedORBIT abstains, loses utility, or becomes ineligible.
- **REQ-2001** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A solver that reaches a configured time/resource limit with a valid state/bound artifact yields terminal execution state `Completed` and method outcome `Time Limit` or `Resource Limit`.
- **REQ-2002** (§18; Failure Semantics) — No higher-resource retry is allowed for a solver-limit outcome in the same scientific experiment.
- **REQ-2003** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A correctly invoked scientific algorithm unable to produce its required certificate for reasons other than time/resource limit terminates as `Failed / Scientific Algorithmic Failure`.
- **REQ-2004** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Treat `Sparse Master Non-Convergence` as `Failed / Scientific Algorithmic Failure` for FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-2005** (§18; Artifact) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must still produce numerical diagnostics.
- **REQ-2006** (§18; Artifact) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must record failure reason.
- **REQ-2007** (§18; Artifact) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must record completed-support records.
- **REQ-2008** (§18; Artifact) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must record cut/master counters.
- **REQ-2009** (§18; Artifact) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must record provenance.
- **REQ-2010** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must not produce a certified action.
- **REQ-2011** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must not proceed to confirmation.
- **REQ-2012** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must not proceed to assimilation.
- **REQ-2013** (§18; Failure Semantics) — A scientific-algorithmic-failure cell must not proceed to TEST scoring.
- **REQ-2014** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Do not automatically retry scientific algorithmic failure with a larger cut cap.
- **REQ-2015** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Do not automatically retry scientific algorithmic failure with a changed tolerance.
- **REQ-2016** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Do not automatically retry scientific algorithmic failure with a different support.
- **REQ-2017** (§18; Failure Semantics) — Do not automatically retry scientific algorithmic failure with an alternate solver.
- **REQ-2018** (§18; Statistical Analysis) — Paired statistical contrasts treat scientific-algorithmic-failure cells as missing under §13.6.

- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Expose only roadmap-required invocation, planning, status, validation, rendering, and error-translation behavior.
- Convert boundary primitives immediately to typed domain values; do not embed scientific logic in command handlers.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Consume the validated typed scientific configuration and existing domain contracts. Add or extend only typed domain/schema structures required by the covered requirements; do not introduce new scientific constants, alternate defaults, or shadow configuration authority.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: CLI/E2E tests prove exact command semantics, no-op reuse, selective overwrite, and descendant validity behavior.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- When the covered requirements produce persisted evidence, write only canonical roadmap-required outputs through the artifact/provenance contract with the required schema, integrity, dependency, validity, and completion metadata; downstream reporting must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

# M02 — I11 Implement Semantic Cells, Fingerprints, Selective Invalidation, and Recovery

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M02 — Deterministic Execution, Artifact, and Provenance Backbone
- **Primary deliverable:** Semantic-cell execution graph with dependency fingerprints, staleness, invalidation, crash safety, and recovery.
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure
- **Requirement coverage:** 183 total (182 implementation-bearing; 1 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §20

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-2545–REQ-2727

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-2545** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `experiment` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2546** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `dataset` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2547** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `source_client` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.

- **REQ-2549** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `directed_pair` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2550** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `method` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2551** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `condition` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2552** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `support` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2553** (§20.1; Provenance) — Use `seed` as a scientific semantic-cell identity coordinate when scientifically relevant to the experiment.
- **REQ-2554** (§20.1; Provenance) — Include only dimensions scientifically relevant to a given experiment in its semantic identity.
- **REQ-2555** (§20.1; Provenance) — UUIDs must not define scientific identity.
- **REQ-2556** (§20.1; Provenance) — timestamps must not define scientific identity.
- **REQ-2557** (§20.1; Provenance) — incrementing run numbers must not define scientific identity.
- **REQ-2558** (§20.1; Provenance) — random IDs must not define scientific identity.
- **REQ-2559** (§20.1; Provenance) — hash-only IDs must not define scientific identity.
- **REQ-2560** (§20.1; Provenance) — Treat hashes and timestamps only as provenance/compatibility information, not scientific identity.
- **REQ-2561** (§20.1; Reproducibility) — A rerun of the same valid semantic cell is the same scientific result.
- **REQ-2562** (§20.1; Artifact) — Shared-artifact reusable identity is determined by artifact type, semantic producer coordinates, and dependency fingerprint, not by the first requesting experiment.
- **REQ-2563** (§20.2; Provenance) — Every reusable artifact must have exactly one `dependency_fingerprint_sha256` computed only from dependencies capable of materially changing that artifact.
- **REQ-2564** (§20.2; Provenance) — Include exact upstream artifact identities consumed in an artifact dependency fingerprint when applicable.
- **REQ-2565** (§20.2; Provenance) — Include applicable scientific configuration subset in an artifact dependency fingerprint when applicable.
- **REQ-2566** (§20.2; Provenance) — Include applicable semantic coordinates including seed when stochastic behavior depends on it in an artifact dependency fingerprint when applicable.
- **REQ-2567** (§20.2; Provenance) — Include registered implementation fingerprint for the producing code path in an artifact dependency fingerprint when applicable.
- **REQ-2568** (§20.2; Provenance) — Include model/generator/preprocessing definition where applicable in an artifact dependency fingerprint when applicable.
- **REQ-2569** (§20.2; Provenance) — Include stage-specific numerically material runtime/ABI fingerprint where changes can affect produced values in an artifact dependency fingerprint when applicable.
- **REQ-2570** (§20.2; Provenance) — Implementation fingerprints must be stage-local and cover the producer function/module plus registered transitive scientific code used by that producer.
- **REQ-2571** (§20.2; Provenance) — Do not use the whole repository commit as the implementation fingerprint.
- **REQ-2572** (§20.2; Provenance) — Numerically material runtime fingerprints must be stage-local.
- **REQ-2573** (§20.2; Provenance) — Preprocessing runtime fingerprints include exact parsing/serialization/numeric libraries that affect preprocessing output.
- **REQ-2574** (§20.2; Provenance) — Training runtime fingerprints include framework/CUDA/library components that affect training numerics.
- **REQ-2575** (§20.2; Provenance) — Solver runtime fingerprints include solver backend/version and relevant numerical libraries.
- **REQ-2576** (§20.2; Provenance) — Changes to plotting/document-export dependencies must not invalidate scientific artifacts.
- **REQ-2577** (§20.2; Provenance) — Record complete repository commit as provenance even when it is not a stage-specific invalidation input.
- **REQ-2578** (§20.2; Provenance) — Record dependency lock as provenance even when it is not a stage-specific invalidation input.
- **REQ-2579** (§20.2; Provenance) — Record operating system as provenance even when it is not a stage-specific invalidation input.
- **REQ-2580** (§20.2; Provenance) — Record hardware as provenance even when it is not a stage-specific invalidation input.
- **REQ-2581** (§20.2; Provenance) — Record driver as provenance even when it is not a stage-specific invalidation input.
- **REQ-2582** (§20.2; Provenance) — Record environment as provenance even when it is not a stage-specific invalidation input.
- **REQ-2583** (§20.2; Provenance) — A provenance component invalidates an artifact only when a stage-specific dependency rule includes it because it can alter computation or interpretation.
- **REQ-2584** (§20.2; Provenance) — Changing any dependency included in a fingerprint creates a different compatible-artifact key.
- **REQ-2585** (§20.2; Provenance) — Changing material outside an artifact's fingerprint must not invalidate that artifact.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue must trace to the roadmap authority above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy it.

## Objective

Deliver Semantic-cell execution graph with dependency fingerprints, staleness, invalidation, crash safety, and recovery so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§20 — Semantic-cell identity, fingerprints, provenance, staleness, invalidation, and recovery.**
  - Required verification: Fingerprint/provenance tests detect meaningful dependency changes, preserve unaffected ancestors, and recompute from the nearest valid boundary.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Preserve every listed `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` requirement as a scope, terminology, theorem-assumption, exclusion, falsification, or claim constraint; do not turn it into artificial production behavior.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- **M02 — I07 Implement Deterministic RNG and Reproducibility Identity** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Deterministic seed namespaces, replay behavior, and reproducibility/environment identity.
- **M02 — I08 Implement Canonical Artifact Reuse and Completion Manifests** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Reusable-artifact and completion manifests with dependency-aware immutable artifact reuse.
- **M02 — I09 Implement Failure Taxonomy, Retry, and Scientific Failure Semantics** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Typed failure states, retry behavior, and scientific/infrastructure failure handling.

### Blocks

- **M02 — I12 Implement Canonical Workspace, Serialization, and Provenance Lifecycle** — provides Semantic-cell execution graph with dependency fingerprints, staleness, invalidation, crash safety, and recovery as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Canonical computational workspace and validated artifact/provenance lifecycle.
- **M02 — I13 Implement Ordered Execution Pipeline and Execution-Readiness Gates** — provides Semantic-cell execution graph with dependency fingerprints, staleness, invalidation, crash safety, and recovery as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Layered restartable execution pipeline and M02 readiness verification.
- **M03 — I14 Enforce Strict No-Common-Interface Resource Boundary** — provides Semantic-cell execution graph with dependency fingerprints, staleness, invalidation, crash safety, and recovery as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Whitelisted strict-resource interface with dynamic access validation and readiness gates.

Dependencies describe the actual contract or evidence exchanged between issues; dependency completion alone is insufficient unless the consumed output is valid, current, provenance-compatible, and scientifically admissible.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Semantic-cell identity, fingerprints, provenance, staleness, invalidation, and recovery.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Add or extend only the typed immutable domain/configuration contracts required by the covered requirements.
- Validate cross-field invariants and reject unknown or scientifically invalid values before execution.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Expose only roadmap-required invocation, planning, status, validation, rendering, and error-translation behavior.
- Convert boundary primitives immediately to typed domain values; do not embed scientific logic in command handlers.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Fingerprint/provenance tests detect meaningful dependency changes, preserve unaffected ancestors, and recompute from the nearest valid boundary.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

## Objective

Deliver Canonical computational workspace and validated artifact/provenance lifecycle so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§21 — Canonical computational workspace and active artifact layout.**
  - Required verification: Artifact-layout/schema/checksum tests prove canonical paths, payload identity, manifest completeness, and prohibition of active alternate artifacts.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.

- **M07 — I37 Implement Deterministic Synthetic and Controlled Generators** — provides Canonical computational workspace and validated artifact/provenance lifecycle as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Registered synthetic/exhaustive/coupling/map/scalability generators with deterministic serialization.

Dependencies describe the actual contract or evidence exchanged between issues; dependency completion alone is insufficient unless the consumed output is valid, current, provenance-compatible, and scientifically admissible.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Canonical computational workspace and active artifact layout.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Add or extend only the typed immutable domain/configuration contracts required by the covered requirements.
- Validate cross-field invariants and reject unknown or scientifically invalid values before execution.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Expose only roadmap-required invocation, planning, status, validation, rendering, and error-translation behavior.
- Convert boundary primitives immediately to typed domain values; do not embed scientific logic in command handlers.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Artifact-layout/schema/checksum tests prove canonical paths, payload identity, manifest completeness, and prohibition of active alternate artifacts.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

- **REQ-0903** (§5.5; Reproducibility) — Use the `anonymous_node_order` RNG namespace for node anonymization.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue must trace to the roadmap authority above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy it.

## Objective

Deliver Whitelisted strict-resource interface with dynamic access validation and readiness gates so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§1.2 — Strict no-common-interface information regime.**
  - Required verification: Architecture/resource tests prove that only the roadmap-whitelisted source/target resources are accessible.
- **§5 — Strict resource whitelist, access-control boundary, dynamic access logging, and invalid-cell semantics.**
  - Required verification: Static and dynamic resource-access scans prove each method reads only permitted resources; any violation marks the scientific cell invalid.
- **§26 — Strict-resource readiness and overall implementation-readiness state.**
  - Required verification: The strict-resource enforcement readiness test passes; together with valid M01/M02 readiness evidence, the roadmap implementation-readiness state remains `Pass` before downstream scientific execution.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Preserve every listed `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` requirement as a scope, terminology, theorem-assumption, exclusion, falsification, or claim constraint; do not turn it into artificial production behavior.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.

## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Strict no-common-interface information regime; Strict resource whitelist, access-control boundary, dynamic access logging, and invalid-cell semantics; Strict-resource readiness and overall implementation-readiness state.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Add or extend only the typed immutable domain/configuration contracts required by the covered requirements.
- Validate cross-field invariants and reject unknown or scientifically invalid values before execution.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Architecture/resource tests prove that only the roadmap-whitelisted source/target resources are accessible.
- Automate the milestone verification contract: Static and dynamic resource-access scans prove each method reads only permitted resources; any violation marks the scientific cell invalid.
- Automate the milestone verification contract: The strict-resource enforcement readiness test passes; together with valid M01/M02 readiness evidence, the roadmap implementation-readiness state remains `Pass` before downstream scientific execution.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

# M03 — I15 Implement Duplicate-Safe Chronological Splits and Transfer Eligibility

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M03 — Data Preparation and Strict Resource Interface
- **Primary deliverable:** Deterministic duplicate-safe chronological splitting and source/target transfer eligibility.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 30 total (30 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.3

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0144–REQ-0173

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0144** (§4.3; Dataset) — A transfer concept is source-eligible only when both source TRAIN and source META support thresholds pass.
- **REQ-0145** (§4.3; Dataset) — A transfer concept is target-eligible only when target META, CONFIRM, and TEST support thresholds all pass.
- **REQ-0146** (§4.3; Dataset) — A concept absent or below the applicable support threshold becomes a null transfer node for that endpoint.
- **REQ-0147** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Assign duplicate groups within each retained local prediction class chronologically by duplicate-group midpoint fraction using the configured TRAIN/META/VALID/CONFIRM/TEST intervals.
- **REQ-0148** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — A candidate feature is one raw semantic feature remaining after label, timestamp, identity, payload/provenance, and Edge-specific exclusions, before imputation, missing-indicator creation, scaling, categorical expansion, or constant-feature removal.
- **REQ-0149** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Compute each candidate feature's TRAIN missing/nonfinite fraction at the raw semantic-feature level before imputation or encoding.
- **REQ-0150** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Drop a candidate feature only when its TRAIN missing/nonfinite fraction is strictly greater than the configured feature-quality threshold.
- **REQ-0151** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Invalidate a client only when `dropped_candidate_features / candidate_features_before_quality_filtering` is strictly greater than the configured client-invalidity threshold.
- **REQ-0152** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Construct a missingness indicator only for a retained feature whose pre-imputation TRAIN missing rate is at least the configured missing-indicator threshold.
- **REQ-0153** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Map a TRAIN categorical level to `<RARE>` only when its TRAIN frequency is below the configured rare-category threshold.
- **REQ-0154** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Count each raw candidate feature exactly once in the client-invalidity denominator regardless of later one-hot columns or missingness indicators.
- **REQ-0155** (§4.3; Failure Semantics) — A client with zero candidate features after mandatory semantic exclusions is `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-0156** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — The categorical token identities, comparison directions, quantile rule, categorical ordering, and one-hot semantics are fixed and not configurable.
- **REQ-0157** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — The case-insensitive missing-token vocabulary is exactly: empty string, `0`, `0.0`, `nan`, `none`, `null`.
- **REQ-0158** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Treat string forms `0` and `0.0` as missing only for fields declared categorical by the dataset adapter.
- **REQ-0159** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Numeric zero must remain numeric zero.
- **REQ-0160** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — For each categorical feature, order vocabulary as `<ABSENT>`, `<RARE>`, `<UNK>`, then remaining TRAIN categories in ascending UTF-8 byte order.
- **REQ-0161** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Frequency-based categorical vocabulary ordering is forbidden.
- **REQ-0162** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Compute TRAIN-only numeric quartiles with Hyndman-Fan type 7 / linear interpolation.
- **REQ-0163** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — For each numeric feature, robust-scale as `(x - TRAIN median) / IQR`, substitute scale 1 only when TRAIN IQR is zero, and clip to the configured bounds.
- **REQ-0164** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Remove a zero-IQR feature if it is constant across TRAIN after imputation.
- **REQ-0165** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Assign duplicate-group midpoint fractions to `TRAIN` exactly on interval `[0, 0.55)`.
- **REQ-0166** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Assign duplicate-group midpoint fractions to `META` exactly on interval `[0.55, 0.70)`.
- **REQ-0167** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Assign duplicate-group midpoint fractions to `VALID` exactly on interval `[0.70, 0.80)`.
- **REQ-0168** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Assign duplicate-group midpoint fractions to `CONFIRM` exactly on interval `[0.80, 0.90)`.
- **REQ-0169** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Assign duplicate-group midpoint fractions to `TEST` exactly on interval `[0.90, 1.00]`.
- **REQ-0170** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Map retained categorical missing values to the fixed token `<ABSENT>`.
- **REQ-0171** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Map TRAIN categorical levels below the rare-frequency threshold to the fixed token `<RARE>`.
- **REQ-0172** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — Map categorical levels unseen in TRAIN to the fixed token `<UNK>`.
- **REQ-0173** (§4.3; Preprocessing) — One-hot encoding must drop no category.

# M03 — I16 Implement Dataset Registry, Client Construction, Ontology, and Adapters

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M03 — Data Preparation and Strict Resource Interface
- **Primary deliverable:** Immutable raw-data-backed dataset/client registry, hidden ontology, adapters, and observed-value validation.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 206 total (202 implementation-bearing; 4 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.4
- §6

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0194–REQ-0276, REQ-0925–REQ-1047

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0194** (§4.4; Dataset) — Treat actual immutable repository raw files as authoritative for execution; literature counts are validation references only.
- **REQ-0195** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use only official tabular Edge-IIoTset traffic records for the Edge-IIoTset Network Client.
- **REQ-0196** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use `frame.time` or a release-equivalent event timestamp as the expected Edge-IIoTset event-time semantic field.
- **REQ-0197** (§4.4; Dataset) — Remove Edge-IIoTset binary and multiclass label fields from model input.
- **REQ-0198** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use only the ToN-IoT Windows 10 host telemetry component for the Windows host client.
- **REQ-0199** (§4.4; Dataset) — Exclude Windows 7 records from the ToN-IoT Windows 10 host client.
- **REQ-0200** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use `ts` or a release-equivalent timestamp as the expected ToN-IoT Windows 10 event-time semantic field.
- **REQ-0201** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use only Linux process telemetry for the ToN-IoT Linux Process Host Client.
- **REQ-0202** (§4.4; Dataset) — Exclude ToN-IoT Linux disk and memory tables from the Linux process client.
- **REQ-0203** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use `ts` or a release-equivalent timestamp as the expected ToN-IoT Linux process event-time semantic field.
- **REQ-0204** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use only the ToN-IoT network-flow component for the ToN-IoT Network Client.
- **REQ-0205** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use `ts` or a release-equivalent timestamp as the expected ToN-IoT network event-time semantic field.
- **REQ-0206** (§4.4; Dataset) — Accept a release-equivalent renamed timestamp column only when exactly one column has documented timestamp semantics.
- **REQ-0207** (§4.4; Provenance) — Record every accepted timestamp alias in the raw-data manifest.
- **REQ-0208** (§4.4; Dataset) — Require retained-row parse success for an accepted timestamp alias to meet the configured minimum.
- **REQ-0209** (§4.4; Dataset) — Do not use outcome data to select a timestamp alias.
- **REQ-0210** (§4.4; Failure Semantics) — If timestamp alias requirements fail, mark the dataset `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-0211** (§4.4; Dataset) — Interpret naive timestamps as UTC solely for deterministic ordering.
- **REQ-0212** (§4.4; Dataset) — A constant timezone shift must not change within-client chronological ordering.
- **REQ-0213** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use the roadmap's expected multiclass/binary label fields for each component, subject only to the release-equivalent alias rule.
- **REQ-0214** (§4.4; Dataset) — Accept a release-equivalent renamed label field only when exactly one observed column has the documented semantic role.
- **REQ-0215** (§4.4; Provenance) — Record every accepted label alias in the raw-data manifest.
- **REQ-0216** (§4.4; Dataset) — Establish label aliases without examining model outcomes.
- **REQ-0217** (§4.4; Failure Semantics) — If label semantics cannot be uniquely resolved, mark the component `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-0218** (§4.4; Preprocessing) — Canonicalize local multiclass labels before any support decision by Unicode NFC normalization.
- **REQ-0219** (§4.4; Preprocessing) — Canonicalize local multiclass labels by stripping surrounding whitespace.
- **REQ-0220** (§4.4; Preprocessing) — Canonicalize local multiclass labels by Unicode case-folding.
- **REQ-0221** (§4.4; Preprocessing) — Canonicalize local multiclass labels by replacing each maximal run of non-alphanumeric characters with one underscore.
- **REQ-0222** (§4.4; Preprocessing) — Canonicalize local multiclass labels by collapsing repeated underscores and stripping leading/trailing underscores.
- **REQ-0223** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use canonical normal label `normal`.
- **REQ-0224** (§4.4; Dataset) — Never use the binary label field as a model feature.
- **REQ-0225** (§4.4; Failure Semantics) — When a binary field is present, require its observed normal/non-normal partition to be consistent with the multiclass field; otherwise mark the component `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-0226** (§4.4; Dataset) — When official `Description_stats_datasets`/published feature-order metadata is present in the immutable release, use that as canonical adapter feature order.
- **REQ-0227** (§4.4; Dataset) — When official feature-order metadata is absent, use header order from the lexicographically smallest canonical relative-path file in the component.
- **REQ-0228** (§4.4; Dataset) — Require every additional file for a component to contain the same feature-name set after accepted aliases; reorder to canonical order before row processing.
- **REQ-0229** (§4.4; Failure Semantics) — Duplicate column names after normalization make the component `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-0230** (§4.4; Dataset) — Resolve feature type before missing-token normalization.
- **REQ-0231** (§4.4; Dataset) — Official dataset type metadata takes precedence for feature typing.
- **REQ-0232** (§4.4; Dataset) — Treat documented numeric/integer/floating/boolean/duration/counter/rate/size/timestamp-derived measurements as numeric unless separately excluded.
- **REQ-0233** (§4.4; Dataset) — Treat documented string/label/protocol-state/categorical-code/byte-string/textual fields as categorical unless separately excluded.
- **REQ-0234** (§4.4; Dataset) — If official type metadata are absent, classify a permissible behavioral field as numeric only when every non-missing value across the immutable component parses losslessly as IEEE-754 float64; otherwise classify it categorical.
- **REQ-0235** (§4.4; Dataset) — Feature-type inference may use raw values but must not use labels, split membership, model outcomes, or TEST performance.
- **REQ-0236** (§4.4; Dataset) — Assign every raw field exactly one adapter role from: timestamp, multiclass_label, binary_label, behavioral_numeric, behavioral_categorical, forbidden_identity, forbidden_payload, forbidden_provenance.
- **REQ-0237** (§4.4; Dataset) — Classify documented/named IP or MAC addresses, host/device identifiers, process/thread instance identifiers, flow/session identifiers, row/index identifiers, capture/source filenames, and equivalent record identities as `forbidden_identity`.
- **REQ-0238** (§4.4; Dataset) — Classify raw payload/free-text and byte-sequence payload fields as `forbidden_payload`.
- **REQ-0239** (§4.4; Dataset) — Classify source-file, capture, acquisition, or row-provenance fields as `forbidden_provenance`.
- **REQ-0240** (§4.4; Dataset) — Require every non-label/non-timestamp/non-forbidden remaining field to resolve deterministically to `behavioral_numeric` or `behavioral_categorical`.
- **REQ-0241** (§4.4; Dataset) — Apply the published Edge-IIoTset identifier/payload-style exclusion list in addition to the seven benchmark-integrity exclusions when those fields are present.
- **REQ-0242** (§4.4; Provenance) — Remove a field only once even if multiple exclusion rules apply, while recording all applicable exclusion reasons.
- **REQ-0243** (§4.4; Dataset) — Use official ToN-IoT feature-description files as primary type/role metadata.
- **REQ-0244** (§4.4; Dataset) — Exclude ToN-IoT network identifiers such as `src_ip`, `dst_ip`, host/process instance identifiers, and release-equivalent identities under the universal identity rule.
- **REQ-0245** (§4.4; Dataset) — Retain network ports only when official ToN-IoT descriptions define them as behavioral connection attributes rather than endpoint identity.
- **REQ-0246** (§4.4; Dataset) — Always exclude process IDs and equivalent instance keys.
- **REQ-0247** (§4.4; Dataset) — Treat row-count, class-count, timestamp-range, feature-count, and file-count release differences as observed facts that do not by themselves invalidate a component.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue must trace to the roadmap authority above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy it.

## Objective

Deliver Immutable raw-data-backed dataset/client registry, hidden ontology, adapters, and observed-value validation so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§4.4 — Dataset/client registry behavior, immutable raw-data authority, label canonicalization, and observed-value validation.**
  - Required verification: Dataset validators compare configured identities to immutable raw bytes and record observed checksums/counts/schema facts without hardcoding literature values.
- **§6 — Dataset-specific adapters, client construction, preprocessing outputs, validation, and observed dataset facts.**
  - Required verification: `fedorbit preprocess` outputs schema-valid client artifacts and records all roadmap-required observed values/checksums with provenance.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Preserve every listed `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` requirement as a scope, terminology, theorem-assumption, exclusion, falsification, or claim constraint; do not turn it into artificial production behavior.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- **M02 — I12 Implement Canonical Workspace, Serialization, and Provenance Lifecycle** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Canonical computational workspace and validated artifact/provenance lifecycle.
- **M03 — I14 Enforce Strict No-Common-Interface Resource Boundary** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Whitelisted strict-resource interface with dynamic access validation and readiness gates.
- **M03 — I15 Implement Duplicate-Safe Chronological Splits and Transfer Eligibility** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Deterministic duplicate-safe chronological splitting and source/target transfer eligibility.

### Blocks

- **M03 — I18 Persist Dataset, Eligibility, and Semantic-Cell Manifests** — provides Immutable raw-data-backed dataset/client registry, hidden ontology, adapters, and observed-value validation as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Typed dataset, transfer-eligibility, and semantic-cell manifests with provenance.

Dependencies describe the actual contract or evidence exchanged between issues; dependency completion alone is insufficient unless the consumed output is valid, current, provenance-compatible, and scientifically admissible.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Dataset/client registry behavior, immutable raw-data authority, label canonicalization, and observed-value validation; Dataset-specific adapters, client construction, preprocessing outputs, validation, and observed dataset facts.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Add or extend only the typed immutable domain/configuration contracts required by the covered requirements.
- Validate cross-field invariants and reject unknown or scientifically invalid values before execution.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Expose only roadmap-required invocation, planning, status, validation, rendering, and error-translation behavior.
- Convert boundary primitives immediately to typed domain values; do not embed scientific logic in command handlers.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Dataset validators compare configured identities to immutable raw bytes and record observed checksums/counts/schema facts without hardcoding literature values.
- Automate the milestone verification contract: `fedorbit preprocess` outputs schema-valid client artifacts and records all roadmap-required observed values/checksums with provenance.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

# M03 — I17 Implement Leakage-Safe Feature Selection, Deduplication, and Preprocessing

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M03 — Data Preparation and Strict Resource Interface
- **Primary deliverable:** Leakage-safe feature exclusion, duplicate hashing, and deterministic preprocessing pipeline.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 18 total (17 implementation-bearing; 1 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §§4.5–4.6

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0278–REQ-0295

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0278** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `http.request.method` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0279** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `http.referer` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0280** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `http.request.version` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0281** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `dns.qry.name.len` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0282** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `mqtt.conack.flags` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0283** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `mqtt.protoname` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0284** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Exclude `mqtt.topic` from principal Edge model input before categorical encoding.
- **REQ-0285** (§4.5; Preprocessing) — Canonicalize implicated Edge-IIoTset missing spellings before encoding to neutralize the benchmark serialization/provenance artifact.
- **REQ-0286** (§4.5; Claim Boundary) — Treat the Edge-IIoTset leakage safeguard as benchmark-integrity protection, not as a FedORBIT scientific contribution. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0287** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — After labels and timestamp are parsed, remove all forbidden identity and provenance fields before duplicate hashing.
- **REQ-0288** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — Convert every numeric feature to IEEE-754 float64 for canonical hashing.
- **REQ-0289** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — Use one canonical quiet-NaN representation for missing numeric values in canonical hashing.
- **REQ-0290** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — Normalize categorical values with Unicode NFC and UTF-8 before canonical hashing.
- **REQ-0291** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — Serialize canonical rows with Arrow IPC scalar representation in adapter feature order.
- **REQ-0292** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — Define exact duplicate hash as SHA-256 of canonical feature bytes.
- **REQ-0293** (§4.6; Dataset) — Treat duplicate rows differing only in label as conflicting duplicates.
- **REQ-0294** (§4.6; Failure Semantics) — If a duplicate feature group contains more than one local prediction label, mark the dataset `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-0295** (§4.6; Preprocessing) — Never split a duplicate group across data partitions.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue must trace to the roadmap authority above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy it.

# M04 — I19 Implement Modality-Specific Local Models and Base Training

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M04 — Local Models and Procedural Response Packets
- **Primary deliverable:** Deterministic modality-specific classifiers, training loop, checkpoints, and training artifacts.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 48 total (48 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.7
- §4.8

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0296–REQ-0317, REQ-0329–REQ-0354

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0296** (§4.7; Architecture) — Network/flow classifier order is input → Linear(256) → LayerNorm → GELU → Dropout → Linear(128) → LayerNorm → GELU → Dropout → Linear(64) → GELU → Linear(number_of_local_prediction_classes).
- **REQ-0297** (§4.7; Architecture) — Network/flow LayerNorm uses `eps=1e-5`.
- **REQ-0298** (§4.7; Architecture) — Network/flow LayerNorm uses `elementwise_affine=true`.
- **REQ-0299** (§4.7; Reproducibility) — Network/flow GELU uses exact approximation mode (`none`).
- **REQ-0300** (§4.7; Architecture) — Network/flow Dropout probability is the client-selected pilot value.
- **REQ-0301** (§4.7; Architecture) — Network/flow Linear weights use Xavier-uniform initialization with gain 1.
- **REQ-0302** (§4.7; Architecture) — Network/flow Linear biases initialize to zero.
- **REQ-0303** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host classifier order is input → Linear(192) → ReLU → BatchNorm1d → Dropout → Linear(96) → ReLU → Dropout → Linear(48) → ReLU → Linear(number_of_local_prediction_classes).
- **REQ-0304** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host ReLU uses `inplace=false`.
- **REQ-0305** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host BatchNorm1d uses `eps=1e-5`.
- **REQ-0306** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host BatchNorm1d uses `momentum=0.1`.
- **REQ-0307** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host BatchNorm1d uses `affine=true`.
- **REQ-0308** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host BatchNorm1d uses `track_running_stats=true`.
- **REQ-0309** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host evaluation uses accumulated BatchNorm running statistics.
- **REQ-0310** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host Dropout probability is the selected pilot value.
- **REQ-0311** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host Linear weights use Kaiming-uniform initialization with `a=0`, `mode=fan_in`, and `nonlinearity=relu`.
- **REQ-0312** (§4.7; Architecture) — Host Linear biases initialize to zero.
- **REQ-0313** (§4.7; Reproducibility) — Model parameters and forward/backward training use float32.
- **REQ-0314** (§4.7; Reproducibility) — Preprocessing statistics use float64.
- **REQ-0315** (§4.7; Reproducibility) — Response aggregation uses float64.
- **REQ-0316** (§4.7; Reproducibility) — Metric aggregation uses float64.
- **REQ-0317** (§4.7; Reproducibility) — Optimization-model coefficients use float64.
- **REQ-0329** (§4.8; Training) — Use AdamW as the base optimizer.
- **REQ-0330** (§4.8; Training) — Retain the final partial TRAIN minibatch.
- **REQ-0331** (§4.8; Training) — Shuffle TRAIN each epoch.
- **REQ-0332** (§4.8; Training) — Apply global L2 gradient clipping at the configured norm.
- **REQ-0333** (§4.8; Training) — Use no learning-rate scheduler.
- **REQ-0334** (§4.8; Training) — Evaluate VALID after every completed epoch.
- **REQ-0335** (§4.8; Training) — Use VALID macro cross-entropy as the early-stopping and checkpoint-selection metric.
- **REQ-0336** (§4.8; Training) — Stop after the configured patience in completed epochs without at least the configured minimum improvement.
- **REQ-0337** (§4.8; Training) — Select the epoch with minimum VALID macro-CE as the checkpoint.
- **REQ-0338** (§4.8; Training) — Treat checkpoint metric values within the configured tie tolerance as tied and choose the earliest epoch.
- **REQ-0339** (§4.8; Training) — Use zero label smoothing.
- **REQ-0340** (§4.8; Training) — Reduce loss as the weighted arithmetic mean over minibatch examples.
- **REQ-0341** (§4.8; Training) — Apply the configured probability log floor in loss calculations.
- **REQ-0342** (§4.8; Training) — Use DataLoader workers = 0.
- **REQ-0343** (§4.8; Training) — Pin CUDA host memory for GPU training.
- **REQ-0344** (§4.8; Training) — Use `persistent_workers=false`.
- **REQ-0345** (§4.8; Artifact) — Checkpoint payload must include model parameters.
- **REQ-0346** (§4.8; Artifact) — Checkpoint payload must include optimizer state.
- **REQ-0347** (§4.8; Artifact) — Checkpoint payload must include completed epoch.
- **REQ-0348** (§4.8; Artifact) — Checkpoint payload must include RNG states.
- **REQ-0349** (§4.8; Artifact) — Checkpoint payload must include selected hyperparameters.
- **REQ-0350** (§4.8; Artifact) — Checkpoint payload must include TRAIN class weights.
- **REQ-0351** (§4.8; Training) — Set AdamW `AMSGrad=false`.
- **REQ-0352** (§4.8; Training) — Set AdamW `maximize=false`.
- **REQ-0353** (§4.8; Training) — Set AdamW `fused=false`.
- **REQ-0354** (§4.8; Training) — Set AdamW `foreach=false`.

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M04 — Local Models and Procedural Response Packets

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §§4.9–4.10

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0358–REQ-0375

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0358** (§4.9; Experiment) — Run exactly the Cartesian product of the registered learning-rate, weight-decay, and dropout grids for each client.
- **REQ-0359** (§4.9; Experiment) — Run every base-model pilot configuration on exactly the three pilot seeds.
- **REQ-0360** (§4.9; Experiment) — Base-model pilot comprises exactly 12 configurations and 36 pilot fits per client.
- **REQ-0361** (§4.9; Configuration) — The authoritative pilot seed list is only `scientific.randomness.pilot_seeds`; it must not be duplicated under the pilot grid.
- **REQ-0362** (§4.9; Training) — Select pilot configuration first by smallest median VALID macro-CE over the three pilot seeds.
- **REQ-0363** (§4.9; Training) — Break pilot-selection ties second by smallest VALID macro-CE standard deviation.
- **REQ-0364** (§4.9; Training) — Break remaining pilot-selection ties third by learning rate closest to `1e-3`.
- **REQ-0365** (§4.9; Training) — Break remaining pilot-selection ties fourth by smaller weight decay.
- **REQ-0366** (§4.9; Training) — Break remaining pilot-selection ties fifth by smaller dropout.
- **REQ-0367** (§4.9; Testing) — TEST is inaccessible during pilot selection.
- **REQ-0368** (§4.9; Testing) — CONFIRM is inaccessible during pilot selection.
- **REQ-0369** (§4.10; Mathematics) — For TRAIN class `c`, compute raw class weight `omega_c = N/(\|C\| N_c)`.
- **REQ-0370** (§4.10; Mathematics) — Normalize all raw class weights by their TRAIN-example weighted mean so `(1/N) sum_i omega_{y_i}=1`.
- **REQ-0371** (§4.10; Mathematics) — Define per-example base loss as `-omega_{y_i} log(max(p_i(y_i), probability_log_floor))`.
- **REQ-0372** (§4.10; Mathematics) — For minibatch `B`, optimize exactly `(1/\|B\|) sum_i m_{y_i} ell_i`.
- **REQ-0373** (§4.10; Training) — Use minibatch example count, not the sum of class/intervention weights, as the loss denominator.
- **REQ-0374** (§4.10; Training) — For base training use intervention multiplier `m_c=1`.
- **REQ-0375** (§4.10; Training) — Intervention and curriculum multipliers modify fixed class weights without subsequent renormalization.

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M04 — Local Models and Procedural Response Packets

- **Issue type:** Experiment

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.11

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0385–REQ-0404

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0385** (§4.11; Experiment) — Evaluate every registered source-response intervention magnitude × optimizer-step horizon candidate.
- **REQ-0386** (§4.11; Experiment) — Use the configured number of paired schedules per candidate.
- **REQ-0387** (§4.11; Experiment) — Repeat every candidate at half its intervention magnitude with the same replicate schedules.
- **REQ-0388** (§4.11; Algorithm) — For each magnitude, compute pilot replicate derivatives, mean response, and `ddof=1` standard errors using the same paired-shadow equations as §4.12.
- **REQ-0389** (§4.11; Mathematics) — Define pilot derivative discrepancy `D_ba` exactly as the full-vs-half magnitude absolute difference divided by `max(\|Ahat_ba(epsilon/2)\|, useful_response_magnitude_threshold)`.
- **REQ-0390** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Mark pilot entry `(b,a)` useful when the maximum absolute response at full and half magnitude meets the configured useful-response threshold.
- **REQ-0391** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Evaluate linearity only over useful pilot entries.
- **REQ-0392** (§4.11; Algorithm) — For each useful entry, compute sign agreement from full-magnitude replicate estimates as the larger positive-sign or negative-sign fraction.
- **REQ-0393** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Count an exact-zero replicate as disagreement for sign agreement.
- **REQ-0394** (§4.11; Algorithm) — A source-response pilot candidate is eligible only when every shadow state and loss is finite.
- **REQ-0395** (§4.11; Algorithm) — A source-response pilot candidate is eligible only when median `D_ba` over useful entries is at most the configured discrepancy ceiling.
- **REQ-0396** (§4.11; Algorithm) — A source-response pilot candidate is eligible only when median sign agreement over useful entries meets the configured minimum.
- **REQ-0397** (§4.11; Algorithm) — A source-response pilot candidate is eligible only when at least the configured minimum number of intervention columns contain a useful entry.
- **REQ-0398** (§4.11; Algorithm) — A candidate with no useful entries is ineligible.
- **REQ-0399** (§4.11; Mathematics) — Compute pilot score `Q` as the median over useful entries of `\|Ahat\|/(SE + scientific.source_response_pilot.numerical_floor)` minus the configured curvature-penalty coefficient times the median `D_ba`.
- **REQ-0400** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Break source-response pilot ties first by higher `Q`.
- **REQ-0401** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Break remaining source-response pilot ties second by smaller optimizer horizon.
- **REQ-0402** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Break remaining source-response pilot ties third by smaller intervention magnitude.
- **REQ-0403** (§4.11; Algorithm) — Select exactly one source-response configuration per local model family/client before confirmatory packet construction.
- **REQ-0404** (§4.11; Configuration) — Keep the pilot useful-column minimum and final-packet stability minimum as distinct configuration fields even if current values match.
