- **REQ-0006** (§1.1; Architecture) — A source exports an anonymous fine-node procedural-response packet.
- **REQ-0013** (§1.2; Algorithm) — Estimate source-local procedural responses with simultaneous uncertainty bands.
- **REQ-0413** (§4.12; Algorithm) — All source-response and target-local-response shadows update on TRAIN minibatches only.
- **REQ-0414** (§4.12; Evaluation) — Every response risk `R_b(theta)` is evaluated in model evaluation mode on META only.
- **REQ-0415** (§4.12; Metric) — Compute response risk over the fixed retained native classes of transfer concept `b` using the equal-native-class risk definition in §6.4.
- **REQ-0416** (§4.12; Testing) — VALID must never enter a response derivative.
- **REQ-0417** (§4.12; Testing) — CONFIRM must never enter a response derivative.
- **REQ-0418** (§4.12; Testing) — TEST must never enter a response derivative.
- **REQ-0419** (§4.12; Reproducibility) — For each source intervention, positive and negative shadows start from the exact same checkpoint, optimizer state, and RNG state.
- **REQ-0420** (§4.12; Training) — Positive shadow multiplies every base class weight in intervention concept `a` by `1+epsilon_R`.
- **REQ-0421** (§4.12; Training) — Negative shadow multiplies every base class weight in intervention concept `a` by `1-epsilon_R`.
- **REQ-0422** (§4.12; Mathematics) — Compute each paired response derivative exactly as `(R_b(theta^-)-R_b(theta^+))/(2 epsilon_R max(R_b(theta_0), response-risk floor))`.
- **REQ-0423** (§4.12; Mathematics) — Compute response mean as the arithmetic mean over paired replicates.
- **REQ-0424** (§4.12; Mathematics) — Compute response standard error from sample SD with `ddof=1` divided by `sqrt(R)`.
- **REQ-0425** (§4.12; Statistical Analysis) — For each bootstrap resample, resample paired replicate indices with replacement.
- **REQ-0426** (§4.12; Statistical Analysis) — For each response entry in each bootstrap resample, compute bootstrap mean and bootstrap standard error.
- **REQ-0427** (§4.12; Statistical Analysis) — Compute bootstrap `T_q` as the maximum absolute studentized deviation over response entries using the configured SE floor.
- **REQ-0428** (§4.12; Statistical Analysis) — Derive the simultaneous critical quantile probability from the configured confidence level; do not configure it separately.
- **REQ-0429** (§4.12; Statistical Analysis) — Use empirical `higher` interpolation for the max-\|t\| critical quantile.
- **REQ-0430** (§4.12; Statistical Analysis) — Construct simultaneous lower and upper bands as `Ahat ± q * SE`.
- **REQ-0431** (§4.12; Algorithm) — Do not clip final `L`, `U`, or mean-response estimates.
- **REQ-0432** (§4.12; Algorithm) — Mark a final response entry useful only when its absolute mean response meets the configured threshold.
- **REQ-0433** (§4.12; Algorithm) — Mark a final response entry useful only when its simultaneous interval excludes zero.
- **REQ-0434** (§4.12; Algorithm) — Mark a final intervention column useful when it contains at least one useful entry.
- **REQ-0435** (§4.12; Algorithm) — Count final packet stability useful columns using the final-entry useful definition only.
- **REQ-0436** (§4.12; Algorithm) — Compute the configured median band-width / median absolute mean-response ratio over useful entries only.
- **REQ-0437** (§4.12; Failure Semantics) — If the final useful-entry set is empty, the packet fails the final response stability rule.

- **REQ-0023** (§1.4; Claim Boundary) — The principal theorem and method assume one correspondence acting jointly on response rows and columns. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0024** (§1.4; Claim Boundary) — The principal theorem and method assume nonnegative target importance `w`. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0025** (§1.4; Claim Boundary) — The principal theorem and method assume nonnegative curriculum increment `alpha`. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0026** (§1.4; Claim Boundary) — The principal theorem and method assume nonnegative linear curriculum cost `c`. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

- **REQ-0064** (§3; Mathematics) — For each coarse group `g`, define padded block size `n_g = max(m_g^(s), m_g^(t))`.
- **REQ-0065** (§3; Mathematics) — Pad the smaller endpoint in each coarse group with explicit null nodes until source and target each have `n_g` nodes.
- **REQ-0066** (§3; Mathematics) — Define total padded node count `K = sum_g n_g`.
- **REQ-0067** (§3; Mathematics) — Let `G_g` denote the padded node indices in coarse group `g`.
- **REQ-0068** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the admissible correspondence set `Pi = product_g S_{n_g}`.
- **REQ-0069** (§3; Mathematics) — Represent each `P in Pi` as one block-preserving permutation matrix.
- **REQ-0070** (§3; Mathematics) — Represent the source simultaneous lower and upper response matrices as `L,U in R^{K×K}`.
- **REQ-0071** (§3; Mathematics) — Require target importance `w`, curriculum increment `alpha`, and curriculum cost `c` to be coordinatewise nonnegative.
- **REQ-0072** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the action polytope `A = {alpha >= 0: 1^T alpha <= B_alpha, 0 <= alpha_j <= alpha_bar_j}`.
- **REQ-0073** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the support-limited action set `A^(s) = {alpha in A: \|alpha\|_0 <= s}`.
- **REQ-0074** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the map-conditioned objective `J(alpha;P)=w^T P^T L P alpha - c^T alpha`.
- **REQ-0075** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the principal robust action as an argmax over `A^(s)` of the minimum `J(alpha;P)` over all `P in Pi`, using the principal configured support.
- **REQ-0076** (§3; Mathematics) — For permitted support `S`, define `s_g = \|S ∩ G_g\|`.
- **REQ-0077** (§3; Mathematics) — Define active-image assignment count `N_S = product_g (n_g)_{s_g}` with `(n)_r = n!/(n-r)!`.
- **REQ-0078** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the exact orbit `O(L) = {P^T L P : P in Pi}`.
- **REQ-0079** (§3; Mathematics) — Define the entrywise rectangular hull from `ell_kj = min_P (P^T L P)_kj` and `u_kj = max_P (P^T U P)_kj`.
- **REQ-0080** (§3; Mathematics) — For fixed feasible `alpha`, define `h_orb(alpha)=min_P w^T P^T L P alpha`.
- **REQ-0081** (§3; Mathematics) — For fixed feasible `alpha`, define `h_rect(alpha)=w^T ell alpha`.
- **REQ-0082** (§3; Mathematics) — Define fixed-action rectangularization gap `Gamma(alpha)=h_orb(alpha)-h_rect(alpha)` and require `Gamma(alpha) >= 0`.
- **REQ-0083** (§3; Mathematics) — For experiment-specific action set `B`, define `V_exact(B)=max_{alpha in B} h_orb(alpha)-c^T alpha`.
- **REQ-0084** (§3; Mathematics) — For experiment-specific action set `B`, define `V_rect(B)=max_{alpha in B} h_rect(alpha)-c^T alpha`.
- **REQ-0085** (§3; Mathematics) — Define robust coupling value gap `G_coupling(B)=V_exact(B)-V_rect(B)`.
- **REQ-0086** (§3; Mathematics) — Define `V(P;B)=max_{alpha in B} J(alpha;P)`.
- **REQ-0087** (§3; Mathematics) — Define `V_pre(B)=max_{alpha in B} min_{P in Pi} J(alpha;P)`.
- **REQ-0088** (§3; Mathematics) — Define `V_post(B)=min_{P in Pi} V(P;B)`.
- **REQ-0089** (§3; Mathematics) — Define exact-map action value `Delta_map(B)=V_post(B)-V_pre(B)`.
- **REQ-0090** (§3; Algorithm) — Unless an experiment explicitly requests the dense action set, mechanism and map-value diagnostics must use the principal sparse action set.
- **REQ-0091** (§3; Mathematics) — Null source nodes must have zero response rows.
- **REQ-0092** (§3; Mathematics) — Null source nodes must have zero response columns.
- **REQ-0093** (§3; Mathematics) — Null source nodes must have zero source support counts.
- **REQ-0094** (§3; Mathematics) — Null target nodes must have `w=0`.
- **REQ-0095** (§3; Mathematics) — Null target nodes must have `alpha_bar=0`.
- **REQ-0096** (§3; Mathematics) — Null target nodes must have no action eligibility.
- **REQ-0127** (§4.2; Algorithm) — For each actionable target node `j`, set `alpha_bar_j` from `scientific.action.coordinate_cap`.
- **REQ-0128** (§4.2; Algorithm) — For each actionable target node `j`, set `c_j` from `scientific.action.linear_cost_per_actionable_node`.
- **REQ-0129** (§4.2; Algorithm) — For normal or null target nodes, set `alpha_bar_j=0`.
- **REQ-0130** (§4.2; Algorithm) — For normal or null target nodes, set `c_j=0`.
- **REQ-0131** (§4.2; Mathematics) — Treat the explicit zero-action candidate as having objective exactly 0 by the definition of `J`.

- **REQ-0457** (§4.14; Statistical Analysis) — For each confirmation bootstrap resample, sample the configured replicate indices with replacement.

- **REQ-0465** (§4.14; Algorithm) — Accept confirmation only when the lower confidence bound is at least the configured relative macro-CE acceptance threshold.

- **REQ-0474** (§4.14; Reproducibility) — Live assimilation uses the same infinite-pass TRAIN schedule construction.
- **REQ-0475** (§4.14; Training) — Live assimilation consumes exactly the configured accepted-live-assimilation optimizer steps.
- **REQ-0476** (§4.14; Reproducibility) — Never reuse confirmation shadow schedules as live-assimilation schedules.

- **REQ-0478** (§4.15; CLI / Execution) — Reserve the configured target-response diagnostic step budget exclusively for that purpose.
- **REQ-0479** (§4.15; CLI / Execution) — Reserve the configured confirmation-candidate step budget exclusively for up to three confirmation candidates.
- **REQ-0480** (§4.15; CLI / Execution) — Reserve the configured live-assimilation step budget exclusively for live assimilation.
- **REQ-0481** (§4.15; CLI / Execution) — Reserve the configured nontransferable safety budget exclusively as safety reserve.
- **REQ-0482** (§4.15; Mathematics) — Derive the target-response maximum as eight interventions × eight replicate pairs × two shadows × 25 steps.
- **REQ-0483** (§4.15; CLI / Execution) — Unused target-local optimizer budget from one category must not be transferred to another category.
- **REQ-0484** (§4.15; CLI / Execution) — Unused target-local optimizer budget must not be transferred to another method.

# M05 — I27 Implement FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver and Certificates

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M05 — Robust Correspondence, Selection, and Confirmation Engine
- **Primary deliverable:** Exact sparse separator/master implementation with deterministic ties, work counters, and validity certificates.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 40 total (40 implementation-bearing; 0 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.16; §8.3
- §8

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0498–REQ-0506, REQ-1070–REQ-1100

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0498** (§4.16; Algorithm) — Use HiGHS as the exact-sparse robust-master LP backend.
- **REQ-0499** (§4.16; Algorithm) — Use the HiGHS simplex algorithm.
- **REQ-0500** (§4.16; Algorithm) — Enable HiGHS presolve.
- **REQ-0501** (§4.16; Reproducibility) — Disable HiGHS internal parallelism.
- **REQ-0502** (§4.16; Reproducibility) — Use deterministic HiGHS random seed from configuration.
- **REQ-0503** (§4.16; CLI / Execution) — Permit support-level parallel execution only up to the configured concurrent-support limit because supports are scientifically independent.
- **REQ-0504** (§4.16; Algorithm) — When multiple LAP solutions are optimal within the configured LAP tie tolerance, choose the lexicographically smallest assignment by target-row order and source-node pseudonymous ID.
- **REQ-0505** (§4.16; Algorithm) — Library-specific LAP tie behavior is not authoritative.
- **REQ-0506** (§§4.16, 8.2; Algorithm) — Use `solvers.exact_sparse.lap_objective_tie_tolerance` for ties internal to each blockwise LAP, and use `solvers.exact_sparse.action_tie_tolerance` for ties between completed fixed-action separator correspondence objective values before lexicographic selection.
- **REQ-1070** (§8; Mathematics) — For fixed action, define active support `S={j: alpha_j>0}`.
- **REQ-1071** (§8; Algorithm) — Enumerate every block-compatible injective active-image map `sigma:S->[K]`.
- **REQ-1072** (§8; Mathematics) — For each active-image map, compute the registered fixed-active contribution `C0(sigma)`.
- **REQ-1073** (§8; Mathematics) — For each remaining target outcome and unused source node in the same block, compute registered LAP cost `C^sigma_kb`.
- **REQ-1074** (§8; Algorithm) — Solve one minimum-cost LAP for every coarse block with remaining nodes.
- **REQ-1075** (§8; Algorithm) — Combine fixed active images with every blockwise LAP completion into one admissible full correspondence.
- **REQ-1076** (§8; Algorithm) — Choose the full correspondence minimizing the fixed-action objective.
- **REQ-1077** (§8; Metric) — Count `ActiveImageCandidates` exactly as `N_S` per fixed-action separator call.
- **REQ-1078** (§8; Metric) — Count `LAPCalls` exactly as `N_S * sum_g 1[n_g-s_g>0]`.
- **REQ-1079** (§8; Metric) — Count a size-one completion as one LAP call because the same deterministic assignment primitive is invoked.
- **REQ-1080** (§8; Mathematics) — Use the separator work target `O(N_S sum_g n_g^3)`.
- **REQ-1081** (§8; Algorithm) — When separator correspondences tie within configured LAP/action tolerance, compare source images in ascending target pseudonymous-ID order.
- **REQ-1082** (§8; Algorithm) — Select the lexicographically smallest image sequence among tied separator correspondences.
- **REQ-1083** (§8; Algorithm) — For each allowed support coordinate set, solve the robust master over `alpha,z` with `alpha` restricted to that support and all accumulated scenario cuts.
- **REQ-1084** (§8; Algorithm) — Initialize each support master with the lexicographically smallest block permutation after sorting current pseudonymous IDs.
- **REQ-1085** (§8; Algorithm) — At each support-master iteration, solve the LP.
- **REQ-1086** (§8; Algorithm) — Call the exact separator on the LP action.
- **REQ-1087** (§8; Algorithm) — Compute separator objective `v_sep`.
- **REQ-1088** (§8; Algorithm) — Certify the support when `z-v_sep` is within the configured cut tolerance.
- **REQ-1089** (§8; Algorithm) — Otherwise add the returned correspondence as a scenario cut and continue.
- **REQ-1090** (§8; Failure Semantics) — If the configured cut cap is reached, terminate that support as `Sparse Master Non-Convergence` with no certified robust optimum.
- **REQ-1091** (§8; Failure Semantics) — Because principal certification compares every required support, non-convergence of any required support prevents certification of the method cell.
- **REQ-1092** (§8; Failure Semantics) — Never promote an action from an unconverged support, incumbent master, or other support as the principal exact action when a required support fails.
- **REQ-1093** (§8; Algorithm) — Enumerate every actionable coordinate set with size 1 through the configured support budget.
- **REQ-1094** (§8; Algorithm) — Include the zero action as an additional explicit candidate.
- **REQ-1095** (§8; Algorithm) — Remove actual zero-valued coordinates from an optimized action before deterministic action tie rules.

# M05 — I28 Implement Generic Exact-QAP Truth and Comparator Solver

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M05 — Robust Correspondence, Selection, and Confirmation Engine
- **Primary deliverable:** Generic exact-QAP truth/comparator backend with exactness and failure semantics.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 36 total (33 implementation-bearing; 3 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.17

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0512–REQ-0547

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0512** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Use SCIP through PySCIPOpt for Generic Exact QAP.
- **REQ-0513** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Enable SCIP presolve.
- **REQ-0514** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Enable SCIP cuts.
- **REQ-0515** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Enable SCIP primal heuristics.
- **REQ-0516** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Use binary assignment variables for exact QAP.
- **REQ-0517** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Use exact RLT/McCormick product linearization for QAP products.
- **REQ-0518** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Define `p_aj=1` to mean target padded node `j` maps to source padded node `a`.
- **REQ-0519** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Create assignment variables only for source/target nodes in the same coarse group.
- **REQ-0520** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Enforce exactly one source assignment for each target node within each coarse block.
- **REQ-0521** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Enforce exactly one target assignment for each source node within each coarse block.
- **REQ-0522** (§4.17; Algorithm) — For fixed action, introduce `y_abkj = p_ak p_bj` for every coefficient with nonzero `w_k alpha_j L_ab`.
- **REQ-0523** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Enforce `0 <= y_abkj <= p_ak` for exact product linearization.
- **REQ-0524** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Enforce `0 <= y_abkj <= p_bj` for exact product linearization.
- **REQ-0525** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Enforce `y_abkj >= p_ak + p_bj - 1` for exact product linearization.
- **REQ-0526** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Minimize the registered fixed-action QAP response objective over `p,y`.
- **REQ-0527** (§4.17; Mathematics) — Treat `-c^T alpha` as constant during correspondence separation and add it only when reporting full `J(alpha;P)`.
- **REQ-0528** (§4.17; Comparator) — When Generic Exact QAP is a transfer method, solve the same principal sparse robust-action problem as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0529** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same support enumeration as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0530** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same action polytope as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0531** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same robust-master cuts as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0532** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same zero-action candidate as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0533** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same action tie rules as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0534** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same confirmation and assimilation rules as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0535** (§4.17; Comparator) — Generic Exact QAP uses the same target compute budget as FedORBIT Exact-Sparse Solver.
- **REQ-0536** (§4.17; Comparator) — The only Generic Exact QAP method substitution is replacing the active-image + LAP fixed-action separator with the certified Generic Exact QAP separator.
- **REQ-0537** (§4.17; Algorithm) — Every master-candidate Generic Exact QAP separator result must have a SCIP optimal certificate before it can be used as an exact cut or stopping certificate.
- **REQ-0538** (§4.17; Failure Semantics) — If any required Generic Exact QAP separator reaches its time/resource limit without an optimal certificate, terminate the method cell as `Time Limit` or `Resource Limit`.
- **REQ-0539** (§4.17; Failure Semantics) — Never promote a time/resource-limited QAP incumbent as an exact robust action.
- **REQ-0540** (§4.17; Failure Semantics) — Do not produce downstream confirmation or TEST results after an uncertified required QAP separator call.
- **REQ-0541** (§4.17; Claim Boundary) — Treat Generic Exact QAP as a solver-method comparator, not as a different scientific transfer objective. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0542** (§4.17; Comparator) — Implement Point-Correspondence Commitment QAP through the permutation-invariant Frobenius expansion `\|\|L_s\|\|_F^2 + \|\|L_t\|\|_F^2 - 2<P^T L_s P,L_t>`.
- **REQ-0543** (§4.17; Comparator) — For point correspondence, minimize the equivalent quadratic-assignment term `-2<P^T L_s P,L_t>` using the same binary assignment/product linearization.
- **REQ-0544** (§4.17; Comparator) — Point-correspondence ties use the registered point-map tie tolerance and lexicographic correspondence rule.
- **REQ-0545** (§4.17; Failure Semantics) — A QAP run is exact only when SCIP returns an optimal certificate satisfying the configured MIP gap and feasibility tolerance.
- **REQ-0546** (§4.17; Claim Boundary) — A time-limited QAP incumbent must never be relabeled exact. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0547** (§4.17; Claim Boundary) — Generic Exact QAP registered uses are limited to exact small/medium comparator cases, listed method-level robust-action comparison, point-map structural matching, certified exactness verification, and applicability/map-recovery diagnostics. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

# M05 — I29 Implement FedORBIT Dense-CCP Fallback

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M05 — Robust Correspondence, Selection, and Confirmation Engine
- **Primary deliverable:** Non-exact Dense-CCP fallback with deterministic starts, projection, CCP/master behavior, and scope labeling.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 52 total (46 implementation-bearing; 6 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.18

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0556–REQ-0607

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0556** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Dense-CCP uses the full dense action set `A` with no L0 support restriction.
- **REQ-0557** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Use the same assignment orientation as Generic Exact QAP but relax assignment variables to `[0,1]`.
- **REQ-0558** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Keep blockwise row/column assignment equalities exact in the dense relaxation.
- **REQ-0559** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Introduce lifted `y` variables for every nonzero coefficient in the dense relaxation.
- **REQ-0560** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Apply the same McCormick inequalities to dense lifted variables.
- **REQ-0561** (§4.18; Mathematics) — Define unpenalized dense fixed-action LP objective `F_alpha(p,y)` exactly as the registered response term.
- **REQ-0562** (§4.18; Claim Boundary) — Treat the unpenalized dense lifted optimum `v_relax(alpha)` only as a lower bound on the true fixed-action worst-correspondence response term. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0563** (§4.18; Mathematics) — Define assignment integrality penalty `phi(p)=sum p_aj(1-p_aj)`.
- **REQ-0564** (§4.18; Mathematics) — Use the registered affine majorization `phi_lin(p;p^(t))` at each CCP iterate.
- **REQ-0565** (§4.18; Algorithm) — At each penalty level, solve the LP minimizing `F_alpha + lambda phi_lin` under the continuous lifted constraints.
- **REQ-0566** (§4.18; Mathematics) — Scale penalties by `M=max(1,max \|w_k alpha_j L_ab\|)`.
- **REQ-0567** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Use exactly the configured penalty multiplier ladder relative to `M`.
- **REQ-0568** (§4.18; Metric) — Define assignment integrality residual as `max_{a,j} min(p_aj,1-p_aj)`.
- **REQ-0569** (§4.18; Metric) — Define CCP relative objective convergence using consecutive unpenalized `F_alpha` values and denominator `max(1,\|F_alpha^(t)\|)`.
- **REQ-0570** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Stop a penalty-level trajectory before its iteration cap only when both objective-convergence and integrality-residual criteria pass.
- **REQ-0571** (§4.18; Algorithm) — If either CCP stopping criterion fails, execute the configured maximum iterations and continue to the next penalty level from the last iterate.
- **REQ-0572** (§4.18; Artifact) — Record whether the final penalty level met both CCP convergence criteria.
- **REQ-0573** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Use one blockwise uniform barycenter as deterministic dense start 1.
- **REQ-0574** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Use the lexicographically smallest admissible block permutation as deterministic dense start 2.
- **REQ-0575** (§4.18; Reproducibility) — Generate up to three additional unique permutation starts from the `dense_start` namespace by independently shuffling source-node order within each block and pairing with ascending target pseudonymous order.
- **REQ-0576** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Use at most five dense starts total and at most four permutation starts.
- **REQ-0577** (§4.18; Algorithm) — If the orbit contains fewer than four unique permutations, use every unique permutation exactly once in lexicographic order after deduplication.
- **REQ-0578** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Each dense start must execute the complete penalty ladder.
- **REQ-0579** (§4.18; Algorithm) — The final iterate of each penalty level initializes the next penalty level.
- **REQ-0580** (§4.18; Algorithm) — After every complete CCP trajectory, project final `p` to the nearest admissible block permutation by solving independent maximum-weight LAPs in each block.
- **REQ-0581** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Use the deterministic LAP tie rule from §4.16 during dense projection.
- **REQ-0582** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Evaluate the unpenalized correspondence objective on each projected permutation.
- **REQ-0583** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Choose the projected correspondence with the smallest unpenalized fixed-action objective.
- **REQ-0584** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Break ties between projected correspondences using the global lexicographic correspondence rule.
- **REQ-0585** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Initialize the dense robust-action outer master with the lexicographically smallest admissible block permutation.
- **REQ-0586** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Solve the dense master `max_{alpha,z} z` over `alpha in A` with one cut for every accumulated projected permutation.
- **REQ-0587** (§4.18; Algorithm) — For each dense master action, solve the unpenalized lifted correspondence LP to obtain `v_relax`.
- **REQ-0588** (§4.18; Algorithm) — For each dense master action, run every deterministic CCP start and project every trajectory.
- **REQ-0589** (§4.18; Algorithm) — For each dense master action, select the lowest-objective projected permutation.
- **REQ-0590** (§4.18; Algorithm) — For each dense master action, evaluate full `J(alpha;P_proj)`.
- **REQ-0591** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Add a new projected permutation as a scenario cut only when it is new and violates the master value by more than the exact-sparse separator/cut tolerance.
- **REQ-0592** (§4.18; Algorithm) — Otherwise terminate the dense outer loop with heuristic convergence.
- **REQ-0593** (§4.18; Failure Semantics) — Terminate dense outer loop at heuristic convergence, configured outer-cut cap, configured wall-time cap, or solver/resource failure, whichever occurs first.
- **REQ-0594** (§4.18; CLI / Execution) — Apply the dense wall-time cap to the complete method cell, including master LPs, lifted relaxation solves, CCP trajectories, and projections.
- **REQ-0595** (§4.18; Artifact) — At the returned dense action, record master action and master objective.
- **REQ-0596** (§4.18; Artifact) — At the returned dense action, record the best admissible projected worst-correspondence objective.
- **REQ-0597** (§4.18; Artifact) — At the returned dense action, record the unpenalized lifted relaxation lower bound.
- **REQ-0598** (§4.18; Metric) — At the returned dense action, record `Dense Bound Gap = projected response objective - relaxation lower bound`.
- **REQ-0599** (§4.18; Metric) — At the returned dense action, record assignment integrality residual.
- **REQ-0600** (§4.18; Metric) — At the returned dense action, record outer cut count.
- **REQ-0601** (§4.18; Artifact) — At the returned dense action, record CCP convergence state.
- **REQ-0602** (§4.18; Artifact) — At the returned dense action, record timeout/resource state.
- **REQ-0603** (§4.18; Claim Boundary) — Treat the projected dense permutation only as a feasible correspondence objective for the returned action. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0604** (§4.18; Claim Boundary) — Treat the unpenalized dense lifted LP only as a fixed-action relaxation lower bound. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0605** (§4.18; Claim Boundary) — Neither dense projected objective nor dense relaxation bound may certify the global dense robust optimum. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0606** (§4.18; Claim Boundary) — Dense-CCP never establishes dense exactness or supplies exactness truth. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0607** (§4.18; Claim Boundary) — Dense-CCP registered uses are limited to dense-support sensitivity, fallback diagnostics, and scalability comparisons. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

# M06 — I33 Implement Canonical Predictive, Mechanism, Confirmation, and Efficiency Metrics

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M06 — Comparator, Metric, and Statistical Evaluation Framework
- **Primary deliverable:** Single canonical metric layer including map/action diagnostics and solver/confirmation/efficiency measures.
- **Issue type:** Evaluation
- **Requirement coverage:** 82 total (79 implementation-bearing; 3 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §1.2
- §12

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0017, REQ-1162–REQ-1242

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0017** (§1.2; Evaluation) — Produce correspondence/action diagnostics that separate map identifiability from action certifiability.
- **REQ-1162** (§12; Metric) — All final metrics must come from one registered metric library.
- **REQ-1163** (§12; Reporting) — Table code must not reimplement metric definitions.
- **REQ-1164** (§12; Reporting) — Figure code must not reimplement metric definitions.
- **REQ-1165** (§12; Metric) — Define class-conditional cross-entropy as the mean `-log(max(p_i(c), probability_log_floor))` over examples of class `c`.
- **REQ-1166** (§12; Metric) — Define macro cross-entropy as the arithmetic mean of class-conditional CE over the fixed evaluation class set.
- **REQ-1167** (§12; Failure Semantics) — A fixed evaluation class with zero evaluation examples makes the cell `Invalid Data`.
- **REQ-1168** (§12; Metric) — Define relative macro-CE gain as `(CE_b-CE_m)/max(CE_b, relative denominator floor)`.
- **REQ-1169** (§12; Metric) — If reference macro-CE is below the configured relative denominator floor, report relative gain as `NA`.
- **REQ-1170** (§12; Metric) — When reference macro-CE is below the relative denominator floor, report absolute CE difference.
- **REQ-1171** (§12; Claim Boundary) — A cell with reference macro-CE below the relative denominator floor cannot establish a relative-gain claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-1172** (§12; Metric) — Define per-class precision as `TP/(TP+FP)`.
- **REQ-1173** (§12; Metric) — Define per-class recall as `TP/(TP+FN)`.
- **REQ-1174** (§12; Metric) — Define per-class F1 as `2PR/(P+R)`.
- **REQ-1175** (§12; Metric) — Return zero for any zero denominator in precision, recall, or F1.
- **REQ-1176** (§12; Metric) — Define macro-F1 as the arithmetic mean over the fixed evaluation class set.
- **REQ-1177** (§12; Metric) — Define balanced accuracy as the arithmetic mean of per-class recall over the fixed evaluation class set.
- **REQ-1178** (§12; Metric) — Report the principal certified robust action objective as `Certified robust predicted value`.
- **REQ-1179** (§12; Metric) — Report `Gamma(alpha)` as `Fixed-action rectangularization gap`.
- **REQ-1180** (§12; Metric) — Report `G_coupling` as `Robust coupling value gap`.
- **REQ-1181** (§12; Metric) — Define coupling upper-bound diagnostic as `max_{alpha in B} w^T(bar L-ell)alpha`.

## Objective

Deliver Single canonical metric layer including map/action diagnostics and solver/confirmation/efficiency measures so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§1.2 — Map-identifiability versus action-certifiability diagnostics.**
  - Required verification: Canonical evaluation records separately expose map-identification and action-certification diagnostics without conflation.
- **§12 — Canonical predictive, transfer, coupling, confirmation, map-value, fairness, and efficiency metrics.**
  - Required verification: Metric unit tests on hand fixtures reproduce every formula, denominator rule, aggregation scope, and efficiency field exactly.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Preserve every listed `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` requirement as a scope, terminology, theorem-assumption, exclusion, falsification, or claim constraint; do not turn it into artificial production behavior.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §4.19
- §11

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-0609–REQ-0652, REQ-1132–REQ-1158

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0609** (§4.19; Comparator) — Local-Only performs no transfer and evaluates only the target-local fixed base checkpoint.
- **REQ-0610** (§4.19; Comparator) — Local-SIR uses the target TRAIN/META response artifact and maximizes `w^T L_t alpha - c^T alpha` over the same principal sparse action set.
- **REQ-0611** (§4.19; Comparator) — Local-SIR receives the same action budget, support, confirmation, live-assimilation, and target compute cap as FedORBIT.
- **REQ-0612** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation is identical to principal FedORBIT through source-packet validation, target importance, robust action construction, positive-value filtering, and deterministic source ranking.
- **REQ-0613** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation must not read CONFIRM and must execute no confirmation shadows.
- **REQ-0614** (§4.19; Comparator) — If FedORBIT Without Confirmation has at least one positive proposal, select the first proposal in the same ranking order the principal method would attempt.
- **REQ-0615** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation must return to the same clean pre-transfer target checkpoint/optimizer/RNG state before applying its proposal.
- **REQ-0616** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation applies the selected proposal's curriculum weights.
- **REQ-0617** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation executes the same configured live-assimilation step count using the same `assimilation_schedule` derivation coordinates.
- **REQ-0618** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation opens TEST only after assimilation and the normal pre-TEST artifact contract passes.
- **REQ-0619** (§4.19; Comparator) — If FedORBIT Without Confirmation has no positive proposal, remain Local-Only.
- **REQ-0620** (§4.19; Comparator) — FedORBIT Without Confirmation may not transfer unused confirmation-step reservation to live assimilation or other computation.
- **REQ-0621** (§4.19; Comparator) — For Target Confirmation and Portability, FedORBIT Without Confirmation is the authoritative no-confirm counterfactual and supplies `noConfirmCounterfactualGain` for the corresponding principal proposal/decision.
- **REQ-0622** (§4.19; Comparator) — Matched-Resource Rectangular constructs entrywise lower response `ell_kj=min_P(P^TLP)_kj` and optimizes the same sparse curriculum against `w^T ell alpha-c^T alpha`.
- **REQ-0623** (§4.19; Comparator) — Point-Correspondence Commitment chooses the exact-QAP structural map minimizing `\|\|P^T L_s P-L_t\|\|_F^2`.
- **REQ-0624** (§4.19; Comparator) — Point-Correspondence Commitment breaks ties within the registered tolerance by lexicographically smallest correspondence.
- **REQ-0625** (§4.19; Comparator) — Point-Correspondence Commitment optimizes the curriculum action under the committed map only.
- **REQ-0626** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coarse Block-Mean computes each ordered real-source coarse-block mean `B_gh` from `L`.
- **REQ-0627** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coarse Block-Mean lifts `B_gh` to every target fine-space coordinate according to target coarse groups.
- **REQ-0628** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coarse Block-Mean keeps null target coordinates at zero action cap.
- **REQ-0629** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coarse Block-Min computes each ordered real-source coarse-block minimum `B^min_gh` from `L`.
- **REQ-0630** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coarse Block-Min lifts `B^min_gh` identically to target fine space.
- **REQ-0631** (§4.19; Comparator) — For both coarse summaries, define an ordered source coarse-block pair with no real source entry as exactly zero rather than evaluating an empty-set mean/minimum.
- **REQ-0632** (§4.19; Comparator) — Orbit-Mean uses the uniform average of `P^TLP` over admissible correspondences.
- **REQ-0633** (§4.19; Comparator) — Compute Orbit-Mean analytically blockwise rather than enumerating the orbit.
- **REQ-0634** (§4.19; Comparator) — Orbit-Mean cross-group terms use the mean of all entries in the corresponding source block pair.
- **REQ-0635** (§4.19; Comparator) — Orbit-Mean same-group diagonal target positions use the mean source-block diagonal.
- **REQ-0636** (§4.19; Comparator) — Orbit-Mean same-group off-diagonal target positions use the mean source-block off-diagonal.
- **REQ-0637** (§4.19; Comparator) — Optimize Orbit-Mean action against the mean matrix without a robust minimum.
- **REQ-0638** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coupling-Destroyed packet processes each ordered coarse block pair independently.
- **REQ-0639** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coupling-Destroyed packet vectorizes corresponding `L` and `U` entries in row-major order.
- **REQ-0640** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coupling-Destroyed packet derives one deterministic permutation per ordered block pair from the packet seed namespace.

- **REQ-0645** (§4.19; Comparator) — Coupling-Destroyed packet must preserve empirical upper-value multisets.

## Objective

Deliver Predefined paired statistical framework, multiplicity families, equivalence/materiality, and insufficient-evidence behavior so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§§4.23–4.25 — Statistical behavior, multiplicity families, materiality/equivalence rules, and mechanical claim criteria.**
  - Required verification: Statistical tests reproduce configured alpha/CI/bootstrap/randomization/Holm/materiality criteria and claim-gate decisions without redefining constants.
- **§13 — Paired experimental unit, BCa intervals, exact randomization, equivalence, materiality, multiplicity, missingness, and synthesis rules.**
  - Required verification: Statistical golden tests and exhaustive small fixtures match registered procedures, effective sample handling, family sizes, and correction rules.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Preserve every listed `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` requirement as a scope, terminology, theorem-assumption, exclusion, falsification, or claim constraint; do not turn it into artificial production behavior.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Statistical behavior, multiplicity families, materiality/equivalence rules, and mechanical claim criteria; Paired experimental unit, BCa intervals, exact randomization, equivalence, materiality, multiplicity, missingness, and synthesis rules.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Add or extend only the typed immutable domain/configuration contracts required by the covered requirements.
- Validate cross-field invariants and reject unknown or scientifically invalid values before execution.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Statistical tests reproduce configured alpha/CI/bootstrap/randomization/Holm/materiality criteria and claim-gate decisions without redefining constants.
- Automate the milestone verification contract: Statistical golden tests and exhaustive small fixtures match registered procedures, effective sample handling, family sizes, and correction rules.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

# M07 — I37 Implement Deterministic Synthetic and Controlled Generators

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M07 — Pre-Confirmatory Validation and Solver Benchmarking
- **Primary deliverable:** Registered synthetic/exhaustive/coupling/map/scalability generators with deterministic serialization.
- **Issue type:** Implementation
- **Requirement coverage:** 61 total (60 implementation-bearing; 1 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §14

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-1364–REQ-1424

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-1364** (§§14.1–14.2; Reproducibility) — All synthetic generators use NumPy `Generator(PCG64)` seeded through the `synthetic_instance` namespace.
- **REQ-1365** (§§14.1–14.2; Reproducibility) — All generated matrix and weight computations use float64.
- **REQ-1366** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator draws each `L_ab` iid Uniform(-0.20,0.20).
- **REQ-1367** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator creates serialization-only `U_ab=L_ab+H_ab` with `H_ab` iid Uniform(0,0.05).
- **REQ-1368** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator must not use `U` as separator truth.
- **REQ-1369** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator draws target-importance auxiliaries iid Gamma(shape=2,scale=1).
- **REQ-1370** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator normalizes Gamma auxiliaries to sum-one target importance.
- **REQ-1371** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator selects support uniformly from supports of the required cardinality.
- **REQ-1372** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Exact-separator theorem generator draws active action coordinates iid Uniform(0.05,0.25).
- **REQ-1373** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — If theorem-generator active action sum is at most 0.50, retain drawn values unchanged.
- **REQ-1374** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — If theorem-generator active action sum exceeds 0.50, scale active values proportionally to total 0.50.
- **REQ-1375** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Set theorem-generator coordinates outside the selected support to zero.
- **REQ-1376** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Use the project action cost in theorem-generator fixtures.
- **REQ-1377** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Define theorem-generator truth by exhaustive enumeration of every block permutation for registered small theorem patterns.
- **REQ-1378** (§§14.1–14.2; Experiment) — Do not use a generic solver to define theorem truth when exhaustive enumeration is available.
- **REQ-1379** (§14.3; Experiment) — Coupling generator draws unconstrained response matrix entries iid Uniform(-0.10,0.10).
- **REQ-1380** (§14.3; Experiment) — Coupling generator computes symmetric component `(R+R^T)/2`.
- **REQ-1381** (§14.3; Experiment) — Coupling generator applies configured asymmetry as `(1-a)S+aR`.
- **REQ-1382** (§14.3; Experiment) — Within each ordered coarse block pair, coupling generator centers entries around their block-pair mean and multiplies deviations by configured heterogeneity.
- **REQ-1383** (§14.3; Experiment) — Coupling generator applies exact deterministic sparsity by retaining `max(1, round(q K^2))` coordinates and zeroing all others.
- **REQ-1384** (§14.3; Reproducibility) — Coupling generator ranks sparsity coordinates by SHA-256 over the exact `FedORBIT\|synthetic-sparsity\|baseSeed\|canonicalCoordinates\|a\|b` encoding.
- **REQ-1385** (§14.3; Reproducibility) — Coupling sparsity `canonicalCoordinates` includes generator name, compatibility, heterogeneity, asymmetry, sparsity, block pattern, support, seed, and instance index using canonical JSON.
- **REQ-1386** (§14.3; Reproducibility) — Interpret the full SHA-256 sparsity digest as an unsigned big-endian integer for ranking.
- **REQ-1387** (§14.3; Reproducibility) — Break any coupling sparsity digest tie by ascending coordinate `(a,b)`.
- **REQ-1388** (§14.3; Reproducibility) — Do not use RNG draws or library hash functions for coupling sparsity selection.
- **REQ-1389** (§14.3; Experiment) — Draw coupling-generator `w` and `alpha` by the theorem-generator rules.
- **REQ-1390** (§14.3; Algorithm) — For every positive-weight active term, compute the exact set of orbit permutations attaining its marginal minimum.
- **REQ-1391** (§14.3; Experiment) — Classify a coupling fixture as `jointly_realizable` only when the intersection of all positive-weight active-term minimizer sets is nonempty.
- **REQ-1392** (§14.3; Experiment) — Classify a coupling fixture as `incompatible` only when that minimizer-set intersection is empty and fixed-action rectangularization gap exceeds the configured strict threshold.
- **REQ-1393** (§14.3; Experiment) — Use rejection sampling until the requested coupling structural class is obtained.
- **REQ-1394** (§14.3; Failure Semantics) — If the configured maximum attempts cannot construct the requested coupling class, return `Generator Failure` and block that designed-family experiment.
- **REQ-1395** (§14.3; Failure Semantics) — Never silently weaken a failed coupling-generator structural criterion.
- **REQ-1396** (§14.4; Experiment) — Common-action unresolved-map generator uses block pattern `(2,2)`.
- **REQ-1397** (§14.4; Experiment) — Set every response within a coarse block pair to the same sampled `beta_gh`.
- **REQ-1398** (§14.4; Experiment) — Draw each `beta_gh` from the configured Uniform(0.04,0.12) range.
- **REQ-1399** (§14.4; Experiment) — Use configured Gamma-normalized target weights in common-action fixtures.
- **REQ-1400** (§14.4; Experiment) — Preserve all four blockwise maps as admissible while ensuring `P^TLP=L` for every map.
- **REQ-1401** (§14.4; Experiment) — Require the common action to have positive robust value; reject a generated fixture that does not.
- **REQ-1402** (§14.5; Experiment) — Robust-compromise unresolved-map generator uses block pattern `(2,2)`.
- **REQ-1403** (§14.5; Experiment) — Draw robust-compromise `L_ab` from the configured Uniform(-0.10,0.20) range.
- **REQ-1404** (§14.5; Experiment) — Draw robust-compromise target importance using the configured rule.
- **REQ-1405** (§14.5; Experiment) — Use the principal sparse action set in robust-compromise fixtures.
- **REQ-1406** (§14.5; Experiment) — Accept robust-compromise fixture only when more than one admissible correspondence exists.
- **REQ-1407** (§14.5; Experiment) — Accept robust-compromise fixture only when the intersection of map-conditioned optimal-action sets is empty within action tie tolerance.
- **REQ-1408** (§14.5; Experiment) — Accept robust-compromise fixture only when robust pre-map value exceeds the configured threshold.
- **REQ-1409** (§14.6; Experiment) — Map-dependent generator uses block pattern `(2,2)`.
- **REQ-1410** (§14.6; Experiment) — Draw map-dependent `L_ab` from the configured Uniform(-0.15,0.25) range.
- **REQ-1411** (§14.6; Experiment) — Accept map-dependent fixture only when `Delta_map` meets the configured minimum.
- **REQ-1412** (§14.6; Experiment) — On a valid map-dependent fixture, FedORBIT must select a lower-valued compromise or abstain.
- **REQ-1413** (§14.6; Claim Boundary) — FedORBIT must never output semantic map certainty in map-dependent boundary fixtures. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-1414** (§14.7; Experiment) — Zero-map-value fixture family uses the common-action generator.
- **REQ-1415** (§14.7; Experiment) — High-map-value fixture family uses the map-dependent generator.
- **REQ-1416** (§14.7; Experiment) — Both map-bound fixture families use the principal sparse action set.
- **REQ-1417** (§14.8; Experiment) — For each scalability `K`, balanced blocks are `(floor(K/2), ceil(K/2))`.
- **REQ-1418** (§14.8; Experiment) — For each scalability `K`, maximally skewed two-block pattern is `(K-1,1)`.
- **REQ-1419** (§14.8; Experiment) — Scalability generator draws `L_ab` iid Uniform(-0.10,0.10).
- **REQ-1420** (§14.8; Experiment) — Scalability generator uses uniform target importance `w_k=1/K`.
- **REQ-1421** (§14.8; Experiment) — For fixed-action scalability timing at support `s`, choose the first `s` pseudonymous nodes in the largest block.
- **REQ-1422** (§14.8; Experiment) — Set each selected scalability action coordinate to `min(0.25,0.50/s)`.
- **REQ-1423** (§14.8; Artifact) — Every synthetic scalability cell records fixed-action separator metrics.
- **REQ-1424** (§14.8; Artifact) — Every synthetic scalability cell records full registered robust-action solver metrics where applicable.

- **REQ-0794** (§4.26; Reproducibility) — Deterministic kernel timing uses exactly the configured warmup count.
- **REQ-0795** (§4.26; Reproducibility) — Deterministic kernel timing uses exactly the configured timed repetition count.
- **REQ-0796** (§4.26; Metric) — Primary runtime summaries report median and p95.
- **REQ-0797** (§4.26; Reproducibility) — Full training executions are timed once per scientific cell.
- **REQ-0798** (§4.26; Reproducibility) — Training must not be repeated merely to manufacture timing samples.
- **REQ-1711** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Classify Scalability and Efficiency as `Robustness / EFFICIENCY`.
- **REQ-1712** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Use the registered K grid, balanced and maximally skewed block patterns, supports 1/2/3 for exact/QAP, no support cap for dense, and all ten confirmatory seeds.
- **REQ-1713** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Plan 960 synthetic exact/QAP cells.
- **REQ-1714** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Plan 160 synthetic dense cells.
- **REQ-1715** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Plan 1,120 total synthetic solver cells.
- **REQ-1716** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Plan 120 real primary timing cells before deterministic exclusions.
- **REQ-1717** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Robustness) — Use the authoritative timing warmup/repetition protocol.
- **REQ-1718** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Metric) — Define predicted work coordinate `X=N_S sum_g n_g^3` for each fixed-action exact-sparse scalability cell.
- **REQ-1719** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — Within each block-pattern × support stratum with enough distinct non-timeout K values, compute Spearman correlation between `log X` and `log` median exact-sparse runtime.
- **REQ-1720** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — Efficiency-trend component passes only when every eligible stratum has Spearman rho > 0.
- **REQ-1721** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Claim Boundary) — The scalability Spearman correlation is descriptive and receives no p-value threshold.
- **REQ-1722** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — A stratum with fewer than the configured minimum points is `Insufficient Trend Evidence` and cannot establish the runtime-trend component.
- **REQ-1723** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — Work-structure claim requires every truth-valid exact-sparse cell's Active-Image Candidates to equal `N_S`.
- **REQ-1724** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — Work-structure claim requires every truth-valid exact-sparse cell's LAP Calls to equal the exact formula in §8.1.
- **REQ-1725** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — Work-structure claim requires no approximation to replace a required exact separator.
- **REQ-1726** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Statistical Analysis) — Work-structure claim requires the runtime-trend component to pass.
- **REQ-1727** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Claim Boundary) — Exact counters passing with insufficient/nonpositive runtime trend yields at most `Partially Supported`.
- **REQ-1728** (§15 — Scalability and Efficiency; Claim Boundary) — Any counter mismatch or required approximation yields `Not Supported`.

# M09 — I51 Implement Immutable Kill and Simplification Rules

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M09 — Statistical Synthesis, Claim Adjudication, and Manuscript Evidence
- **Primary deliverable:** Mechanical non-neutralizable kill/simplification rules over verified experiment evidence.
- **Issue type:** Validation
- **Requirement coverage:** 67 total (46 implementation-bearing; 21 `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` governing constraints).

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §17

### Requirements

- **Requirement IDs:** REQ-1923–REQ-1989

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-1923** (§17 — Exactness Failure; Evaluation) — Trigger on any reproducible exact-sparse objective error above exactness tolerance or invalid correspondence certificate.
- **REQ-1924** (§17 — Exactness Failure; Claim Boundary) — Stop every exact-sparse-dependent claim; debug implementation; a mathematical counterexample requires redesign rather than tolerance inflation. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-1925** (§17 — Rectangularization Is Sufficient; Evaluation) — Trigger when at least 90% of valid real-packet units have absolute coupling gap below configured materiality and no primary pair satisfies coupling mechanism criteria.

The following atomic requirements are the executable authority for this issue. `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` entries are preserved only as governing constraints and do not create fictitious implementation scope.

- **REQ-0004** (§1.1; Claim Boundary) — FedORBIT is the only project/algorithm name used for the contribution. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0005** (§1.1; Claim Boundary) — FedORBIT operates under a cross-schema federated procedural-transfer setting with incompatible raw telemetry, potentially different feature spaces and arbitrary local models, only a shared coarse semantic partition, no exact fine-label correspondence, and no sharing of raw samples, parameters, embeddings, aligned entities, or executable common queries. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0030** (§1.5; Claim Boundary) — The paper must not claim generic action-identifiability theory as new. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0031** (§1.5; Claim Boundary) — The paper must not claim generic non-rectangular robust optimization as new. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0032** (§1.5; Claim Boundary) — The paper must not claim generic QAP, RLT, McCormick, CCP, assignment-polytope, or linear-assignment machinery as new. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0033** (§1.5; Claim Boundary) — The paper must not claim dense exactness. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

- **REQ-0039** (§1.5; Claim Boundary) — The paper must not claim validity outside the tested telemetry families, support regimes, semantic partitions, and strict information interface. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0040** (§2 — Exact Sparse Separator Exactness; Claim Boundary) — Determine whether sparse correspondence separation returns the exact worst admissible correspondence. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0041** (§2 — Exact Sparse Separator Exactness; Claim Boundary) — Exact-sparse and available exact truth must agree within the configured exact-validation tolerance. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0042** (§2 — Exact Sparse Separator Exactness; Claim Boundary) — Any reproducible discrepancy above tolerance or invalid correspondence certificate falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0043** (§2 — Joint Correspondence Avoids Rectangular Pessimism; Claim Boundary) — Determine whether preserving one joint correspondence avoids impossible marginal worst-case combinations. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0044** (§2 — Joint Correspondence Avoids Rectangular Pessimism; Claim Boundary) — Designed incompatible worlds and a nontrivial fraction of real packets must show material positive coupling gap, and coupling destruction must remove the mechanism. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0045** (§2 — Joint Correspondence Avoids Rectangular Pessimism; Claim Boundary) — Failure of the real/synthetic mechanism criteria or mechanism retention after destruction falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0046** (§2 — Action Certification Without Fine-Map Identification; Claim Boundary) — Determine whether useful action can be certified while the fine map remains unresolved. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0047** (§2 — Action Certification Without Fine-Map Identification; Claim Boundary) — Controlled worlds must exist with multiple admissible maps and either a common useful optimum or a positive robust compromise. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0048** (§2 — Action Certification Without Fine-Map Identification; Claim Boundary) — Positive action consistently requiring exact map recovery or failure of the map-value bound falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0049** (§2 — Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility; Claim Boundary) — Determine whether FedORBIT improves target utility under the strict interface. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0050** (§2 — Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility; Claim Boundary) — Principal FedORBIT must materially improve macro cross-entropy relative to Local-Only on the registered majority of primary directed pairs without material harm on another pair. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0051** (§2 — Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility; Claim Boundary) — Failure of the registered utility criteria or strict-resource validation falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0052** (§2 — Value of External Procedural Evidence; Claim Boundary) — Determine whether the source response packet adds value beyond matched target-local curriculum search. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0053** (§2 — Value of External Procedural Evidence; Claim Boundary) — FedORBIT must materially improve over Local-SIR on the registered majority of primary pairs. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0054** (§2 — Value of External Procedural Evidence; Claim Boundary) — Local-SIR equivalence or superiority under the registered criteria falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0055** (§2 — Operational Relevance of Sparse Support; Claim Boundary) — Determine whether bounded support is practically useful rather than only theoretically convenient. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0056** (§2 — Operational Relevance of Sparse Support; Claim Boundary) — The registered sparse condition must remain close to dense utility on the required proportion of units while retaining useful realized transfer. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-0057** (§2 — Operational Relevance of Sparse Support; Claim Boundary) — The registered sparse-irrelevance rule falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

- **REQ-0060** (§2 — Target Confirmation Safety; Claim Boundary) — Failure of the safety or coverage criteria falsifies the claim. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

- **REQ-1876** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 1: Assign `Not Tested` when required experiments have no scientifically interpretable completed evidence because they were not executed or were blocked before required endpoints.
- **REQ-1877** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 2: Assign `Not Supported` when an explicit failure/falsification condition or claim-negating kill/simplification rule fires.
- **REQ-1878** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 3: Assign `Supported` when the full support rule passes over the full declared scope.
- **REQ-1879** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 4: Assign `Conditional` only where an explicit rule permits pre-outcome data/eligibility scope reduction and positive criteria pass on that reduced scope.
- **REQ-1880** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 5: Assign `Mechanism Only` only where a claim-specific rule permits controlled/theorem mechanism evidence without required real-packet evidence.
- **REQ-1881** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 6: Assign `Partially Supported` only where at least one claim-specific positive component meets its registered materiality/statistical requirement, the full support rule fails, and no explicit failure rule fires.
- **REQ-1882** (§16.1; Evaluation) — Mechanical claim-state precedence step 7: Assign `Null Result` when required evidence is complete, no positive component reaches materiality, and no contradictory/harm/falsification condition fires.
- **REQ-1883** (§16.1; Evaluation) — No final claim state may be selected by narrative judgment.
- **REQ-1884** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Exact Sparse Separator Exactness`: Evaluate `Supported` only over required truth-available cases; truth-unavailable larger benchmark cells do not downgrade the claim.
- **REQ-1885** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Exact Sparse Separator Exactness`: Use `Not Tested` only when required exhaustive/theorem truth evidence is unavailable.
- **REQ-1886** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Exact Sparse Separator Exactness`: Any reproducible exact mismatch or invalid certificate yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1887** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Joint Correspondence Avoids Rectangular Pessimism`: Use `Mechanism Only` when complete designed synthetic/theorem mechanism passes, real-packet materiality is unavailable/not reached, and coupling destruction does not contradict the mechanism.
- **REQ-1888** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Joint Correspondence Avoids Rectangular Pessimism`: Synthetic/theory failure or coupling-destruction retention yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1889** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Action Certification Without Fine-Map Identification`: Use `Partially Supported` when exactly one of common-action or robust-compromise controlled families satisfies its positive construction and the orbit-radius bound remains valid.
- **REQ-1890** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Action Certification Without Fine-Map Identification`: Any bound violation or evidence that exact map recovery is always required yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1891** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility`: Use `Conditional` only when exactly one primary pair was removed before outcome inspection for deterministic invalid-data/eligibility reasons and all three remaining pairs satisfy every registered pair/equal-pair criterion.
- **REQ-1892** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility`: Use `Partially Supported` when one or two full-scope primary pairs satisfy all positive pair criteria, no pair is materially harmful, and strict-resource validation passes.
- **REQ-1893** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility`: Use `Null Result` when no pair is materially beneficial and no pair is materially harmful.
- **REQ-1894** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Strict Cross-Telemetry Transfer Utility`: Any materially harmful pair or strict-resource failure yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1895** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Value of External Procedural Evidence`: Apply the same state logic as strict transfer with Local-SIR as the reference.
- **REQ-1896** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Value of External Procedural Evidence`: Any registered Local-SIR equivalence/superiority that fires the simplification rule yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1897** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Operational Relevance of Sparse Support`: Use `Partially Supported` when at least one registered sparse support has material realized benefit on at least one primary pair but the full sparse rule fails.
- **REQ-1898** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Operational Relevance of Sparse Support`: Use `Null Result` when no sparse support reaches useful-transfer materiality and sparse-irrelevance does not fire.
- **REQ-1899** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Operational Relevance of Sparse Support`: Sparse-irrelevance kill rule yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1900** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Target Confirmation Safety`: Use `Partially Supported` when at least one but fewer than three primary pairs meet ARR/RRR criterion and no pair exceeds harmful-worsening or coverage-loss ceilings.
- **REQ-1901** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Target Confirmation Safety`: Use `Null Result` when no pair meets either harm-reduction threshold and no worsening/coverage failure occurs.
- **REQ-1902** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Target Confirmation Safety`: Any safety/coverage failure or Confirmation Has No Safety Value trigger yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1903** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Sparse Solver Work-Structure Agreement`: Use `Partially Supported` when exact counters and exactness pass but one or more eligible runtime-trend strata are nonpositive or insufficient.
- **REQ-1904** (§16.1; Evaluation) — For `Sparse Solver Work-Structure Agreement`: Any counter mismatch or required approximation yields `Not Supported`.
- **REQ-1905** (§16.1; Claim Boundary) — A pre-outcome pair exclusion must not change any threshold. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-1906** (§16.1; Claim Boundary) — A pre-outcome pair exclusion must not create a replacement pair. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-1907** (§16.1; Claim Boundary) — Any `Conditional` manuscript wording must name the reduced empirical scope explicitly. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**
- **REQ-1908** (§16.1; Claim Boundary) — Final manuscript wording must not exceed the scope allowed by the adjudicated claim state. **[Governing `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` constraint]**

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue must trace to the roadmap authority above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy it.

## Objective

Deliver Claim-state engine preserving contribution scope, research questions, hypotheses, falsification boundaries, evidence sufficiency, and allowed wording so that every implementation-bearing requirement allocated to this issue is executable and objectively verifiable, while every governing constraint is preserved without being misrepresented as new implementation scope.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the referenced roadmap requirements:

- **§§1.1, 1.5; §2 — Contribution identity, strict-scope constraints, forbidden claims, research questions, hypotheses, and falsification boundaries.**
  - Required verification: Claim catalogue and scope tests preserve exact allowed/excluded wording and encode every registered support/falsification condition mechanically.
- **§16 — Allowed claim states, evidence sufficiency, manuscript wording, and scope restriction.**
  - Required verification: Claim-adjudication tests map evidence to only registered states and mechanically constrain manuscript wording to the adjudicated empirical scope.
- Implement the complete behavior stated by every implementation-bearing atomic requirement listed under **Roadmap Authority → Requirements**, including its numerical, ordering, failure, artifact, provenance, execution, statistical, and reporting semantics where applicable.
- Preserve every listed `NON_IMPLEMENTATION` requirement as a scope, terminology, theorem-assumption, exclusion, falsification, or claim constraint; do not turn it into artificial production behavior.
- Expose only the interfaces, artifacts, schemas, CLI behavior, experiment evidence, or reporting surfaces required by these requirements and by declared downstream dependencies.

No requirement may exist only implicitly in acceptance criteria, tests, or implementation notes.
## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- **M06 — I35 Implement Statistical Analysis, Multiplicity, Materiality, and Equivalence** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Predefined paired statistical framework, multiplicity families, equivalence/materiality, and insufficient-evidence behavior.
- **M07 — I42 Validate Coupling Mechanism, Action Certifiability, and Map-Value Boundaries** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Synthetic/real coupling and unresolved-map controlled-world evidence with exact map-value boundaries.
- **M08 — I49 Finalize Confirmatory Experiment Dependencies and Evidence Exposure** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Canonical dependency/output/downstream-exposure map for all confirmatory and robustness experiments.
- **M09 — I50 Perform Statistical Synthesis and Claim-Evidence Aggregation** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Registered paired statistical synthesis and adjudication-ready evidence dependency outputs.
- **M09 — I51 Implement Immutable Kill and Simplification Rules** — consumes its validated primary deliverable: Mechanical non-neutralizable kill/simplification rules over verified experiment evidence.

### Blocks

- **M09 — I53 Generate Verified Publication Tables, Figures, and Manuscript Evidence** — provides Claim-state engine preserving contribution scope, research questions, hypotheses, falsification boundaries, evidence sufficiency, and allowed wording as an upstream contract/evidence dependency for Precision-controlled manuscript-facing tables, figures, source data, and publication evidence from verified artifacts.

Dependencies describe the actual contract or evidence exchanged between issues; dependency completion alone is insufficient unless the consumed output is valid, current, provenance-compatible, and scientifically admissible.
## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Implement the roadmap-defined behavior for: Contribution identity, strict-scope constraints, forbidden claims, research questions, hypotheses, and falsification boundaries; Allowed claim states, evidence sufficiency, manuscript wording, and scope restriction.
- Keep scientific/domain logic out of CLI and presentation layers and preserve repository dependency direction.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Consume the validated typed scientific configuration and existing domain contracts. Add or extend only typed domain/schema structures required by the covered requirements; do not introduce new scientific constants, alternate defaults, or shadow configuration authority.

### Tests

- Automate the milestone verification contract: Claim catalogue and scope tests preserve exact allowed/excluded wording and encode every registered support/falsification condition mechanically.
- Automate the milestone verification contract: Claim-adjudication tests map evidence to only registered states and mechanically constrain manuscript wording to the adjudicated empirical scope.
- Add regression coverage for every defect discovered while implementing the issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Produce only roadmap-required canonical artifacts/evidence with deterministic identity, schema validation, integrity checks, provenance, and completion semantics.
- Reporting or publication surfaces must consume verified persisted evidence rather than recompute or manually copy scientific results.

Exact file placement follows repository architecture unless the roadmap explicitly mandates a path.

## Required Tests

A category that genuinely does not apply must be recorded as `N/A — <reason>` in the completion record rather than silently ignored.
### Issue-Specific Validation

- [ ] Renderer golden tests enforce configured decimal/threshold formatting without changing source scientific values.
- [ ] `fedorbit report` tests prove read-only scientific consumption, schema-valid results outputs, shared verified sources for tables/figures, and no scientific recomputation.
- [ ] Every implementation-bearing requirement's inventory acceptance evidence has been demonstrated by an automated test, validated artifact, deterministic inspection, or other objective evidence appropriate to the requirement.

## Required Outputs

- [ ] **Primary deliverable:** Precision-controlled manuscript-facing tables, figures, source data, and publication evidence from verified artifacts exists and satisfies all covered requirement contracts.
- [ ] **Work-package evidence:** Reporting precision and presentation behavior has the required validation/evidence: Renderer golden tests enforce configured decimal/threshold formatting without changing source scientific values.
- [ ] **Work-package evidence:** Verified results publication and manuscript-facing tables/figures/source data has the required validation/evidence: `fedorbit report` tests prove read-only scientific consumption, schema-valid results outputs, shared verified sources for tables/figures, and no scientific recomputation.
- [ ] Automated test evidence for all applicable required-test categories is present and reproducible.
- [ ] Required completion/provenance evidence identifies the active configuration/protocol, code revision, data/model/upstream dependencies, schema versions, and content digests wherever the roadmap requires them.
- [ ] Any persisted outputs required by the covered requirements are canonical, schema-valid, integrity-checked, provenance-valid, and readable by downstream consumers.
